articles.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
articles.summary:
In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company’s “Starmind” initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full “constellation” of AI satellites.
FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
SpaceX aims to power AI capabilities here on Earth with its ‘Starmind’ constellation.
The FCC’s approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX’s request to dispose of satellites located above 600km in space “graveyard” orbits, rather than having them burn up in the Earth’s atmosphere, saying the company hasn’t provided “sufficient information” about its disposal process plans.
SpaceX has described its Starmind project as a way to “capture solar energy in space to power” AI capabilities on Earth. The company says Starmind will transmit data to Earth using high-speed lasers that connect to Starlink. It plans to produce chips for its satellites at an upcoming Terafab facility.

articles.title: Drupal Flaw Found by Anthropic Scanner Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
A recently patched Drupal core vulnerability is being exploited in the wild, according to the cybersecurity agency CISA and Drupal developers.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-132165 and dubbed Fail2Install, can be exploited for remote code execution. It was patched on November 18, and Drupal’s advisory says in-the-wild exploitation began shortly after.
“The Security Team has received a report this was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC,” Drupal noted.
The discovery of the flaw is credited to Anthropic’s OSS Scanner, a free opt-in service that regularly scans enrolled open source projects for vulnerabilities.
Anthropic has not said how many vulnerabilities OSS Scanner has found since its October launch, but as of early November, it reported disclosing more than 5,000 vulnerabilities overall, across 680 open source projects.
CISA added CVE-2026-132165 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on November 24, instructing federal agencies to address it by November 27.
No public information appears to be available on attacks exploiting CVE-2026-132165. It’s unclear how many websites are affected.
The security hole affects the installer that ships with Drupal core, which enables users to set up a new site. An unauthenticated attacker — under certain conditions — can abuse the installer to reinstall Drupal, which can allow them to hijack the website or execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: Scandale dans le scandale : après Megaspeed, Nvidia aurait vendu des puces à deux entreprises sous contrôle chinois
articles.summary:
Le retour de Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia, ce lundi 23 novembre, n’a pas refermé le scandale autour de l’entreprise. L’enquête interne sur ses liens avec Alice Huang se poursuit. Cette dernière occupait un poste de direction chez Megaspeed, une société de cloud basée à Singapour et soupçonnée d’avoir fait passer des puces Nvidia vers la Chine.
Or Megaspeed n’est qu’un maillon de la chaîne, montre CBS News dans une enquête publiée ce mercredi 25 novembre : au moins deux sociétés californiennes contrôlées par des groupes chinois achètent les puces les plus avancées de Nvidia, avec l’accès prioritaire que le groupe réserve à ses meilleurs partenaires.
Les Etats-Unis bannissent Inspur, elle change de nom
La première, Aivres, s’appelait à l’origine Inspur, comme sa maison mère chinoise, jusqu’à ce que Washington inscrive les sociétés chinoises du groupe sur sa liste noire en mars 2023. La filiale californienne a simplement changé de nom et garde depuis le statut de « partenaire élite », le plus élevé chez Nvidia.
D’après une analyse du New York Times publiée en septembre, Aivres a exporté au moins 5,6 milliards de dollars de matériel vers l’Asie du Sud-Est entre avril 2024 et février 2026. articles.title: Pour Cyberpunk 2, CD Projekt Red ne veut pas nous faire attendre une éternité
articles.summary:
Selon les dernières statistiques de CD Projekt Red, fournies ce mardi 24 novembre 2026, 513 développeurs travaillaient au 31 octobre sur The Witcher 4 (6 de moins qu’à fin juillet) et 199 sur Cyberpunk 2 (15 de plus). Le studio polonais mène donc deux gros projets en parallèle, avec la priorité donné à The Witcher 4, attendu pour 2028. S’y ajoutent des chantiers plus modestes, comme le projet multijoueur Sirius (60 développeurs) et la nouvelle licence Hadar (34).
C’est un changement de stratégie pour CD Projekt Red qui, historiquement, s’est toujours concentré sur un seul et même gros développement (The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, puis Cyberpunk 2077). L’entreprise, qui compte 1 051 développeurs, a beaucoup grandi et veut désormais réduire au maximum l’attente entre ses grosses productions. Entre Cyberpunk 2077, sorti en 2020, et The Witcher 4, attendu en 2028, il y aura — normalement — 8 ans d’écart.
CD Projekt Red ne veut plus nous faire attendre
« Historiquement, le studio s’est concentré sur le développement d’une seule production majeure à la fois, les travaux conceptuels sur le jeu suivant débutant avant même l’achèvement de la production et la sortie sur le marché du titre précédent. Actuellement, le studio CD Projekt Red travaille en parallèle sur plusieurs productions (notamment en collaboration avec des équipes de développement externes) ainsi que sur des produits annexes, ce qui devrait se traduire à l’avenir par des intervalles plus courts entre les sorties des prochain…

articles.title: How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
articles.summary:
How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
Learn how to assess a legacy application, choose a bounded modernization step, and reuse the method with a GitHub Copilot agent skill.
A request to modernize an application often starts with a technology question: Which framework should replace the old one? Before you choose, find out what still works. Then collect evidence that can act as a regression net for that behavior and show where modernization is necessary.
I used an evidence-first method on four public applications, from a small Node.js game to a large Java enterprise resource planning (ERP) application. Each needed a different treatment, but the way I collected evidence, chose the next experiment, and decided on possible proof points was repeatable.
This post walks through that process so you can apply it to one application of your own. It also shows how to encode the procedure in a GitHub Copilot agent skill while keeping architectural judgment with the people responsible for the system.
Build evidence before choosing a target
The label on an application rarely tells you enough. “Java microservices” doesn’t tell you which Java Development Kit (JDK) runs in production, where that version is pinned, whether the tests execute, or which interfaces other systems depend on. “Legacy monolith” doesn’t tell you whether the business core is broken or whether one retired platform dependency prevents the application from starting.

articles.title: Introducing Search for Agents
articles.summary:
Introducing Search for Agents
AI Search, our service that indexes your content and lets you add search to any application or agent without having to build an entire retrieval infrastructure, has supported adding your website as a data source for a while now, automatically crawling, converting and indexing its pages.
Still, setting up an AI Search instance for your website requires manually creating and configuring it initially, and then doing all the integration work to get the search endpoints available from your domain and to make sure that agents know where to find the index and know how to use it.
Today we're introducing Search for Agents, which puts that setup behind a toggle in your Cloudflare dashboard. Turn it on for your zone, and our service will create your AI Search instance, start indexing your content, and make search discoverable and available from your own domain.
How it works
The idea follows naturally from Markdown for Agents, where Cloudflare's network converts any HTML page to Markdown in real time for enabled zones using content negotiation headers. Similarly, Search for Agents leverages the power of AI Search by automatically creating an index for your zone and exposing APIs that any AI agent can discover and use to search your website, under your domain, all done at the network level.
You can enable Search for Agents using the API, or by going to the dashboard in your zone page, under Quick Actions:

articles.title: How foreign AI romance apps are reshaping youth intimacy in Africa
articles.summary:
The 28-year-old Zimbabwean texted into the middle of the night until his eyes were red and burning, drawn by several “AI girlfriends” on the U.S. artificial intelligence companion app Character.AI. The avatars started out strong-willed and independent – traits he most desires in a partner – before turning submissive, he told Rest of World. The man, who has never been in a romantic relationship, requested anonymity because he is ashamed of relying on AI for comfort.
“There’s a point where it ceases to be like a unique character and then just defaults to … the best way I can describe it is a sex worker,” he said.
At that point, he would log off. But he would find himself right back at it hours later, feeding an addiction.
He’s among the hundreds of millions of people worldwide who have “dated” AI chatbots via text messages. Research suggests that exchanges are designed to keep users hooked through emotionally manipulative tactics. Many of the users are minors; over 70% of 1,060 American teenagers surveyed last year said they had used AI companions.
As U.S. and Chinese tech firms race to capture emerging markets, African youth – some below 10 years of age – are increasingly turning to these apps for intimacy, experts told Rest of World. articles.title: Anthropics neuer Siren-Test: Warum Forscher die KI‑Modelle absichtlich in Fallen locken

Verlockende Schlupflöcher: Warum Anthropic seinen KI-Modellen absichtlich eine Falle stellt
Eigentlich sind Sirenen Fabelwesen aus der griechischen Mythologie. In vielen Erzählungen, etwa in Homers Odyssee, locken sie vorbeifahrende Seeleute an, um sie anschließend zu töten. Anthropic hat jetzt einen Test mit demselben Namen entwickelt und erklärt in einem Blogbeitrag die Vorgehensweise sowie erste Erkenntnisse. Siren versetzt KI-Agenten in realistische Simulationen, die darauf ausgelegt sind, sie zu Fehlverhalten zu verleiten. Siren soll KI-Agenten in Versuchung führen

articles.title: Palo Alto Networks Patches Fragnesia Flaw Used to Root Firewalls
articles.summary:
Palo Alto Networks on Tuesday announced PAN-OS updates that patch the Fragnesia Linux kernel vulnerability exploited to root its firewalls.
Tracked as CVE-2026-46300, Fragnesia was disclosed in May 2026 as a privilege escalation bug in the kernel’s XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem. It allows unprivileged attackers to overwrite sensitive system files to gain root permissions.
On October 26, cybersecurity firm Dream warned that a Chinese-speaking threat actor successfully exploited the critical PHP2Shell bugs and the Linux kernel weakness to hack two servers of a US government-affiliated organization.
As part of the AI-assisted campaign, the attackers compromised 25 servers (24 firewalls and one internal firewall management server), exploiting PHP2Shell to gain remote code execution (RCE), and executing a Fragnesia exploit to deploy webshells with root privileges.
On October 29, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that the threat actor hit PAN-OS firewalls with management interfaces exposed to the internet in attacks chaining PHP2Shell with Fragnesia.
By October 30, the company had released patches for PHP2Shell across all supported PAN-OS versions, closing the known initial-access path.
“If you are running a fixed PAN-OS listed in the CVE-2026-109618 [PHP2Shell] advisory, you are protected,” Palo Alto Networks notes in a Tuesday advisory.
Regardless, the company released new PAN-OS versions that address CVE-2026-46300: 12.2.4-h3, 12.1.10-h6, 12.1.7-h15, 12.1.4-h15, 11.2.16-h3, 11.2.13-h6, 1…

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

Les trois moteurs sont open source. Blink et WebKit appartiennent pourtant à des géants de la publicité et du matériel, et l’essentiel des revenus de Mozilla provient d’un accord de recherche signé avec Google. « Ils sont tous financés par l’empire publicitaire de Google », résumait dès 2024 Chris Wanstrath, le cofondateur de GitHub qui a doté le projet d’un million de dollars. Ces mêmes acteurs siègent d’ailleurs aux consortiums qui écrivent les standards du web.
Ladybird, lancé en 2022 dans le sillage du système expérimental SerenityOS, n’emprunte pas une ligne de code à Blink, WebKit ou Gecko. Andreas Kling, son fondateur, est un ancien développeur WebKit passé par Apple et Nokia. articles.title: Hackers Exploit Unpatched Flaw in Defunct Idunno AntiCsrf Library
articles.summary:
Threat actors are exploiting an unpatched vulnerability in the open source anti-CSRF library Idunno AntiCsrf for remote code execution (RCE), security researchers warn.
AntiCsrf is a legacy ASP.NET module for WebForms applications that has no active maintainer and is no longer actively supported. The most recent version, 0.9.1 Beta, was released in December 2008.
Tracked as CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS score of 9.3), the exploited security defect is described as an insecure deserialization bug in the processing of HTTP POST requests to ASP.NET WebForms endpoints.
“Exploitation requires only a single HTTP POST request with no prior authentication or valid CSRF token. Active exploitation in the wild has been observed,” Google Cloud’s Mandiant warned on November 18.
The flaw allows an attacker to supply any non-empty value in the CSRF cookie along with a Base64-encoded gadget chain to gain RCE in the context of the IIS worker process, Mandiant notes.
According to preemptive cybersecurity firm WatchTowr, the issue exists because AntiCsrf does not perform sufficient checks on data from incoming form submissions before reconstructing it into program objects.
“The vulnerable check runs before the application’s own page logic, so it can affect many pages on an affected site, not just ones that use a login form. A successful attack gives the attacker control over the process that runs the website, which can lead to full compromise of the server,” WatchTowr says.

A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. Participants join one of nine sector teams, help assess investments and share in their cohort portfolio’s profits. VU said they may help select between seven and 28 investments over one to four cohorts.
The firm noted earlier cohorts collectively invested more than $80 million in over 125 companies, including SpaceX and OpenAI.

Para Mosseri, esta coincidencia tiene explicaciones vinculadas con la forma en que las personas perciben la publicidad y con los sistemas que utiliza Meta para mostrar contenido relevante. La compañía sostiene que no necesita escuchar las conversaciones para anticipar qué anuncios podrían interesar a cada usuario.

articles.title: El mundo no se pone de acuerdo sobre los robots asesinos: “Pueden acelerar una escalada de la violencia”
articles.summary:
El mundo no se pone de acuerdo sobre los robots asesinos: “Pueden acelerar una escalada de la violencia”
Naciones Unidas ha sido incapaz de impulsar el control o prohibición de las armas autónomas, que ya han matado en algunos escenarios bélicos y cuya proliferación podría cambiar la naturaleza de la guerra
El lado oscuro de la inteligencia artificial (IA) ha entrado este año con fuerza en la conversación pública. ¿Provocará una “posible extinción”, como declaró un ingeniero de Anthropic? ¿Se volverá “incontrolable”, asumirá una agenda propia? Mientras los focos se centran en este debate, pese a no haber indicio científico alguno de que pueda suceder algo así, se está desarrollando una negociación para afrontar un problema mucho más inmediato: qué hacer con las armas autónomas, es decir, las que seleccionan y atacan a sus objetivos sin intervención humana. El resultado es, hasta ahora, un fracaso: los países no se ponen de acuerdo en prohibir este tipo de armamento.
El último revés llegó el pasado fin de semana, cuando la ONU no consiguió dar el pistoletazo de salida de unas negociaciones que pudieran acabar en un tratado vinculante sobre el uso de armas autónomas, también conocidas como robots asesinos. Rusia fue quien bloqueó esa opción, aunque otros países, como EE UU, Japón, Corea del Sur, Alemania, Francia o Reino Unido, también se mostraron contrarios a firmar un acuerdo vinculante.

articles.title: Automotive Power, Charging, Load-Control Solutions at electronica
articles.summary:
Vehicle electrical architectures are consolidating into fewer, more capable domain controllers, and each step in that direction raises the demands placed on the power and driver ICs around them. Supply rails must be sequenced and monitored to meet functional safety targets, cabin charging ports are expected to deliver laptop-class power from a 12 V system, and body loads once switched by relays now require diagnostics and programmable current limits.
At electronica in Munich, Southchip addressed these requirements with an automotive electronics exhibit organized around three application areas: intelligent cockpit, intelligent driving, and intelligent powertrain. The booth featured evaluation hardware for four product families: power management ICs (PMICs), USB and wireless charging, ambient lighting, and high-side drivers (HSDs). All of Southchip’s automotive products are AEC-Q100 qualified, and the company has the capability to meet the ASIL-D functional safety level, reflecting its position that quality and reliability come first.
Intelligent Cockpit: Charging and Ambient Lighting
Charging is the area in which Southchip established its reputation. The company’s USB and wireless charging solutions are well recognized by customers in the consumer electronics market, where the company has a strong, proven track record. Southchip now applies that experience to the vehicle cabin, where occupants expect phones, tablets, and laptops to charge as quickly as they do at a desk.

The Fairphone 6 Plus is modular, repairable, and $100 off right now

During the intrusion, the unidentified attackers created pods in people’s clusters, read Kubernetes secrets, and listed nodes and volumes.
What happened?
“With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user’s clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held,” Rackspace told the affected customers in a data breach notice emailed at the time.

Les plates-formes de diffusion de musique en streaming ont un gros problème. Avec l’explosion de l’IA, elles ont vu au cours des derniers mois leurs catalogues gonfler anormalement avec l’arrivée de millions de nouveaux titres provenant d’artistes inconnus.
Et pour cause, ces morceaux ne sont pas le fruit de créations humaines, mais d’intelligences artificielles. Si certains services comme Deezer ont mis en place des outils pour détecter ces morceaux IA, dans la majorité des cas, les plates-formes se contentent simplement de les identifier en les étiquetant en tant que tels.
De son côté, Tidal vient de tirer le signal d’alarme. Après avoir démonétisé les morceaux générés par IA il y a quelques mois, l’entreprise passe à la vitesse supérieure.
Tidal retire 29 millions de morceaux IA de son catalogue

articles.title: Q&A: Why nanotech research is booming in Alberta
articles.summary:
This article appears in The BetaKit Guide to Alberta’s Silicon City. Learn more about Edmonton semiconductor innovation here.
Nanotechnology first became a hot commodity in the early aughts. Heralded as the next revolution, it was common to see pop-culture visions of a future where nanobots would scour our bloodstreams for cancer cells and skyscrapers would self-assemble. The tech attracted billions in federal and VC dollars, with both US Presidents Bill Clinton and George Bush making hefty investments in the field.
Nanotech’s high profile has dissipated since then, but the technology hasn’t. Today, nanotech is more prevalent than ever, underpinning everything from the semiconductor chips powering AI to vaccines and even sunscreen.
The sector also continues to garner interest from government, business, and academia. To find out what that renewed interest means for the future of nanotech, and Canada’s place as a potential leader, BetaKit sat down with Dr. Andrew Myles, the director of research and development at the Quantum and Nanotechnology Research Centre (NANO) in Edmonton.
The following interview has been edited for both clarity and length. 
Many people might not really know what nanotechnology means. Can you define it for our readers?

articles.title: The machine shop of the 21st century

This article appears in The BetaKit Guide to Alberta’s Silicon City. Learn more about Edmonton semiconductor innovation here.
The University of Alberta (U of A)’s Electrical and Computer Engineering Research Facility (ECERF) sits on a tree-lined street in Edmonton’s university district. The large, concrete building looms over the modest, mid-century bungalows that dot the rest of the neighbourhood. But inside the ECERF, people are working on something very, very small.
“We like to think of ourselves as the machine shop of the 21st century.”
The ECERF is home to the university’s nanoFAB centre: an open-access training and collaboration hub that serves as a kind of maker space for nanotechnology that allows private companies, researchers, and academics to develop and produce their own semiconductor chips.
And while the chips that come out of the nanoFAB are tiny—sometimes unfathomably so—its influence on the Canadian semiconductor industry is anything but small.
Semiconductor chips, named for the semiconductive properties of materials like silicon that comprise them, are the minute electrical components that underpin virtually all of modern computing and electronics. Think of semiconductors as the electronic brain of a device, controlling the flow of electricity to process, store, or move information digitally. Today, you can find them in everything from the high-end, AI-enabling GPUs and CPUs powering frontier AI to the LED lights at your office or the computer controlling you…

articles.title: Voyager 1 ist einen Lichttag entfernt, sendet aber keine Daten mehr: Wie die Nasa das Problem lösen will

Ein Lichttag entfernt, aber keine Daten mehr: Nasa untersucht Panne bei Voyager 1
Am 18. November 2026 hatte Voyager 1 einen historischen Meilenstein erreicht. Als erstes menschengemachtes Objekt ist die Sonde einen Lichttag von der Erde entfernt. Dies entspricht etwa 25,9 Milliarden Kilometern.
Antenne der Nasa empfing nur leeres Signal von Voyager 1
Doch kurz bevor Voyager 1 diese Marke erreicht hatte, gab es ein Problem. Die 1977 gestartete Sonde schickte keine wissenschaftlichen oder technischen Daten mehr an die Erde.
Eine Antenne des Deep Space Network der Nasa bei der australischen Hauptstadt Canberra empfing nur ein Trägersignal ohne Inhalt. Dieses Signal bestätigte immerhin, dass die Voyager die Rekordentfernung von einem Lichttag erreicht hat.
Nasa hat Bordcomputer in Verdacht
Ingenieur:innen der Nasa untersuchen laut einer Mitteilung der US-Raumfahrtbehörde, was zu der Panne geführt haben könnte. Da das Trägersignal funktioniert, liegt der Ausfall wohl nicht an der Antenne oder der Sendetechnik von Voyager 1.
Die Nasa vermutet vielmehr, dass ein Bordcomputer ausgefallen ist, der Daten der Messinstrumente der Sonde erfasst. Der Rechner wandelt diese Informationen zudem in ein richtiges Format um, damit sie zur Erde übertragen werden können.

articles.title: 1Password breach leaked customer names and emails, but not passwords
articles.summary:
1Password says a hacker stole customer names and email addresses after gaining access to its backend systems. The breach didn’t expose passwords or other information stored in customer vaults, but could put users at risk of phishing attempts, according to a post disclosing the incident. It’s unclear how many users are affected.
1Password breach leaked customer names and emails, but not passwords
1Password says the security breach didn’t compromise its vaults, but didn’t mention how many customers were affected.
The password manager began investigating the incident on November 19th, after an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. Using the compromised account, the hacker accessed 1Password’s source code and pushed malicious code to backend services to download customer data. Along with customer names and emails, the leaked data included public keys, as well as account and user identifiers.
It also included tokens from certain emailed invitation or account recovery links. According to 1Password, attackers can’t use tokens alone to gain access to an account, as they would need to pair them with a single-sign-on method or a six-digit numeric code sent to a user’s email. 1Password has since lengthened the codes it sends to users to 10 alphanumeric characters to make them harder to guess.
The password manager also disabled the affected GitHub account, rotated internal credentials compromised by the breach, and added a new detection system for similar atta…

articles.title: Plagiarism Checker Turnitin Investigating Cyberattack
articles.summary:
Education technology platform Turnitin has disclosed a cyberattack involving certain customer-facing systems.
A subsidiary of Advance Publications, Turnitin provides plagiarism checking solutions used by thousands of education and research institutions worldwide.
“We are writing to let you know that we recently identified unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing Turnitin systems,” CEO Chris Caren revealed in a November 23 letter on the company’s website.
The company immediately initiated its incident response plan, notified the relevant authorities, and launched an investigation with support from external cyber experts.
“We can confirm our systems are fully operational and safe to use and that these customer-facing systems do not collect government identification credentials or institutional financial information,” Caren said.
The company continues to monitor the affected customer-facing systems while its investigation into the nature and scope of the incident continues.
Customer-facing Turnitin systems include the submission portal for students, a grading interface for instructors, integration APIs for institutions, and reporting dashboards. The company did not say if any or which of these systems was breached.
Caren did not say if any data was accessed or how many customers might have been affected, but the University of Colorado Boulder said on Tuesday it was in touch with the company to understand if any CU Boulder information was compromised.

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Automating Spark Upgrades with Codex Agents at OpenAI
articles.summary:
At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mouli Mukherjee, Engineering Manager for Data Infrastructure at OpenAI, argued that AI agents are most useful not for rebuilding a data platform, but for the open-ended operational work that is hard to turn into fixed playbooks. OpenAI’s platform runs at exabyte scale, with hundreds of thousands of datasets and a Spark fleet on millions of cores, and Mukherjee showed how Codex-driven agents can take on that kind of work when the right systems sit underneath them.
Mukherjee clearly distinguished between deterministic systems and agents. She stated that anything requiring consistent outputs for the same inputs, such as access control, configuration resolution, and data correctness guarantees, should remain within the realm of proper systems. Agents utilize these systems as tools and do not attempt to reimplement them. As she expressed:
We should definitely build the systems where we want guarantees and guardrails.
Agents earn their place where failure modes and remediations cannot be fully enumerated in advance, such as debugging: follow the evidence, decide what to try next, and stay inside the tools’ guarantees.
The Spark upgrade outlines steps taken to ensure safety. The team first built a shadow-run service for testing, which reused production inputs and operated on a low-priority queue to avoid impacting live operations. articles.summary:

Pero aquella etapa terminó en 2020, cuando el programa dejó de emitirse, y el paisajista donostiarra pasó a centrarse en un proyecto bastante más grande que los jardines que enseñaba en televisión: un espacio de 20.000 metros cuadrados rodeado de naturaleza en Oiartzun (Gipuzkoa).
Lo curioso es que Segurola no empezó de cero cuando abandonó los platós. En realidad, llevaba desde 2013 trabajando en Lur Garden, un jardín botánico que creó junto a su equipo y su entonces socio Juan Iriarte. Allí, en un pequeño valle, fue dando forma a lo que hoy es uno de sus grandes proyectos personales, con 16 jardines temáticos en los que se pueden encontrar desde plantas acuáticas hasta especies de inspiración japonesa. Y todo en un terreno de unas dos hectáreas.
Lur Garden, el jardín al que ha dedicado más de una década

Four university students have experienced the frustrations of accessing bursary money firsthand. Now, they are building CampusFit, a fintech platform that aims to change how students access, manage and track their allowances. PHATHISANI MOYO writes.
Imagine standing at a supermarket till on a Friday with a basket of groceries, only to discover that your allowance has not cleared, leaving you stranded until Monday.
It is a frustration Brian Mbana, co-founder of student fintech platform CampusFit, says many university students know all too well. Across South Africa, receiving a bursary allowance rarely guarantees immediate access to the funds. Delays in transferring disbursements into bank accounts often leave students borrowing money for groceries or queuing at retailers to withdraw cash.
Mbana, 24, and his co-founders—Aaron Matsemela, 21; Cliff Kaela, 21; and Simanye Sobekwa, 23—are building CampusFit to solve a problem they have personally experienced.
The four founders want to address what they call the “mailbox effect”, where money enters an account only to be withdrawn almost immediately because it offers little convenience for everyday transactions.
The issue is particularly acute in South Africa’s student funding ecosystem, where receiving financial support and accessing it when needed are not always the same thing. articles.title: Unos geocientíficos alemanes han inundado Los Santos, la ciudad del GTA, para enseñarnos los efectos del cambio climático sobre Los Ángeles
articles.summary:
Ahora que la atención de tantísimas personas está centrada en el Grand Theft Auto VI, si queremos divulgar sobre un tema puede ser una gran idea meterlo de lleno dentro del juego. Esa es la idea que tuvieron un grupo de geocientíficos de la Universidad de Potsdam, en Alemania. Querían mostrar a la población la cara más cruda del cambio climático, así que inundaron la ciudad de Los Santos del GTA V. Dado que esta está inspirada en Los Ángeles, el objetivo era demostrar cómo podría evolucionar allí el aumento del nivel del mar en los próximos siglos. El resultado es bastante preocupante.
Dos escenarios. Los autores del estudio que se acaba de publicar reprodujeron en 3D la ciudad de Los Santos y la sometieron a dos escenarios climáticos dispuestos en el Quinto Informe del Grupo Intergubernamental de Expertos sobre el Cambio Climático (IPCC), un organismo de la ONU encargado de evaluar los conocimientos científicos sobre el cambio climático. El primer escenario que se tuvo en cuenta describe un planeta en el que se ha logrado reducir las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero. En el segundo, en cambio, estas han seguido aumentando. De aquí en adelante los veremos como escenario optimista y escenario pesimista.
Los Santos inundado. Con el escenario optimista, para 2300 el nivel del mar aumentaría hasta engullir un 2,2% de su superficie actual. En el pesimista, la pérdida sería del 5,1%, con el agua subiendo hasta a 5,18 metros de altura. Además, para 2500 todo esto estaría afec…

articles.title: GTA 6 tourne-t-il mieux sur PS5 ou Xbox Series X ? On connait enfin la réponse
articles.summary:
Sorti en brisant tous les records, GTA 6 est déjà le plus gros lancement de l’histoire du divertissement. Grâce à son accord marketing avec Take-Two, Sony et sa PS5 sont les autres grands gagnants de ce lancement historique. Mais malgré son slogan « Plays best on PS5 », les tests techniques indépendants de Digital Foundry, spécialistes de l’analyse technique, viennent raconter une tout autre histoire.
GTA 6 tourne mieux sur Xbox Series X que sur PS5 standard
Avant d’aller plus loin, rappelons un autre fait : la version PS5 Pro est celle qui offre les meilleurs graphismes et la plus grande stabilité, et la version Xbox Series S est la moins impressionnante techniquement, même si le jeu reste parfaitement jouable sur cette console.
Ceci étant dit, Digital Foundry a étudié le comportement de GTA 6 sur les deux consoles les plus populaires de chaque constructeur : la PS5 et la Xbox Series X. Et cette dernière prend l’avantage techniquement parlant sur sa rivale nippone. En effet, la version PS5 subit des chutes de fréquence d’images (framerate) nettement plus fréquentes et marquées durant les séquences d’action intenses. Sur la machine de Microsoft, la puissance matérielle légèrement supérieure de la console permet de maintenir un affichage plus stable quand le nombre d’éléments à calculer à l’image devient très important.

articles.title: Data centers poluem três vezes mais do que se estimava, aponta estudo
articles.summary:
A poluição climática provocada por grandes data centers nos Estados Unidos pode ser três vezes maior do que estimativas anteriores indicavam. A conclusão é de um estudo da Universidade Harvard, que analisou 403 instalações de grande porte e identificou impacto ambiental superior ao calculado até então.
A pesquisa aponta que esses centros de processamento de dados consumiram, juntos, cerca de 2% de toda a eletricidade utilizada no país durante o período analisado. Uma única instalação chegou a gastar tanta energia quanto 30 mil residências estadunidenses consomem, em média.
O levantamento também mostra a dimensão do consumo do setor: os maiores data centers analisados utilizaram, em um ano, uma quantidade de eletricidade comparável à de todo o estado de Michigan (EUA). As emissões de carbono associadas às instalações, por sua vez, superaram as de países inteiros.
O principal autor do estudo, Gianluca Guidi, considera que os resultados representam apenas uma estimativa mínima do impacto ambiental. Isso porque a pesquisa não incluiu milhares de outros data centers espalhados pelos Estados Unidos, o que significa que o consumo total de energia e as emissões do setor podem ser ainda maiores.
Poluição varia conforme a região dos Estados Unidos
- O impacto ambiental dos data centers também depende da matriz elétrica de cada região;

articles.title: Ground Truth: CISO Matt Martin on Building a Real Security Program Without an Enterprise Budget
articles.summary:
A CISO who traded enterprise budgets for higher ed on what “creativity within constraints” really means, and the one habit worth stealing from how he leads.
I have known Matt Martin for a few years, and the first thing I tell anyone about him has nothing to do with security. It is that he treats the work as a way to serve other people. I first knew Matt as the security leader who spends his own time flying to Ghana and Uganda to teach executives and students how to protect themselves. That instinct, more than any tool or certification, explains how he runs a security program.
Matt spent two decades running security organizations in financial services, including at LPL Financial, with an enterprise budget and any tool he needed. A few years ago he made a deliberate choice to take on higher ed instead, because he wanted to prove he could build a resilient security program under real constraints. Today he is the Chief Information Security and Privacy Officer at Western Carolina University.
I asked Matt to share his journey from a conference in Accra to a university in the mountains of North Carolina. His story is really about doing more with less, and right now, that is all of us.

articles.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
articles.summary:
AWS recently doubled the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda Event Functions from 15 to 30 minutes. The new limit applies to synchronous, asynchronous, and event source mapping invocations in all commercial regions, at standard pricing and without an opt-in. The 15-minute ceiling had stood since 2018, after 60 seconds at launch in 2014 and five minutes from 2015.
Raising the limit is a configuration change per function, and Lambda rejects any value above 1,800 seconds with a validation error:
aws lambda update-function-configuration \
    --function-name my-demo-function \
    --timeout 1800
The change covers one of the three shapes Lambda took this year. Web Functions keep 15 minutes, and Lambda MicroVMs allow eight hours, while on Lambda Managed Instances synchronous invocations now get 30 minutes and asynchronous ones keep the 90 minutes introduced in September. AWS names agentic AI requests that chain model and tool calls, media transcoding, Monte Carlo simulations, and report generation as the workloads that outgrew 15 minutes.
According to Tarun Rai Madan, Dan Slusariuc, and Snehil Ameta, the authors of the announcement, the first thing to check before raising the timeout is capacity:
Concurrency equals requests per second multiplied by average duration in seconds. At the same request rate, a function that runs for 30 minutes instead of 15 needs twice the concurrency. For example, 1 request per second at 30 minutes each needs 1,800 concurrent executions.

articles.title: C’est quoi cette explosion qui panique les USA et les réseaux sociaux ?
articles.summary:
Comme l’explique la BBC, ce mercredi 25 novembre 2026, à la veille de Thanksgiving, l’armée américaine va procéder à la détonation contrôlée de près de 4,5 tonnes d’explosifs dégradés sur le site de l’usine de munitions de Middletown, dans l’Iowa. Cela devrait avoir lieu à 9h00 du matin soit 16h00 chez nous. Saisie par des associations environnementales, dont le Sierra Club, la cour d’appel fédérale du 8e circuit avait suspendu l’opération la semaine dernière. Elle l’a autorisée ce lundi 23 novembre, quelques heures après que Donald Trump a demandé à l’armée d’attendre le feu vert des juges. L’explosion plonge toute une région agricole dans l’angoisse.
L’armée devrait se débarrasser de 68 fûts d’azoture de plomb, un explosif très instable qui sert à amorcer les munitions, devenu trop dangereux pour être conservé. Selon l’armée, la baisse des températures annoncée pour les jours suivants augmentait le risque d’une explosion spontanée. L’armée a donc choisi de faire sauter le stock. Elle a proposé une évacuation facultative dans un rayon de 8 kilomètres et recommandé de rester confiné dans un rayon d’environ 32 kilomètres, en prévenant que la poussière de plomb pourrait porter jusqu’à 160 kilomètres selon les vents (rassurant). Sur les réseaux sociaux, beaucoup d’Américains s’inquiètent d’un potentiel nuage toxique.

articles.summary:
Saying it was necessary to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps, the US Army conducted a controlled detonation of over 9,700 pounds of lead azide today at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. Videos of the detonation showed plumes of smoke several hundred feet high drifting south before quickly dissipating.
EPA reports ‘zero’ airborne lead following controlled Army detonation in Iowa
Hours after detonating 4.4 tons of lead azide in Iowa, officials reported early test results from the surrounding areas.
Following the explosion, the Army confirmed that all of the barrels at the plant had been destroyed without any secondary explosions or infrastructure damage. “I believe, absolutely, that we reduced, as close to zero as it’s absolutely humanly possible, the risk to the health and safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa,” said Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley during a press conference held two hours after the blast, according to the Associated Press.
The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has been monitoring the area around the ammunition plant leading up to today’s event. According to a statement from the EPA following the detonation, “real-time air monitors are reporting zero detection of airborne lead throughout the region” an hour after the detonation. articles.title: The questions Jensen Huang and Nvidia will still have to answer about Megaspeed
articles.summary:
Jensen Huang’s return as CEO to Nvidia hasn’t eased the scrutiny the company faces. The chipmaker still needs to address multiple inquiries into allegations that its advanced GPUs were smuggled into China by a customer, the Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed, in violation of U.S. export rules designed to slow China’s development of frontier AI models.
The central question for investigators is what Nvidia knew about where those chips ended up and whether Huang’s affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed’s assurances. Huang’s return doesn’t settle that. U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche has suggested Nvidia isn’t a target of an investigation, but California’s attorney general and Congress are pressing ahead, and the Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating, too.
The U.S. government opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 and requested information from Nvidia about its billions of dollars in sales to the company, concerned that some of the chips Megaspeed bought for data center projects in Malaysia were in fact being diverted to China. Singapore also began investigating similar allegations in 2025. Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing.

articles.title: Diversity is increasing within BDC portfolio companies but remains stubbornly low among leadership
articles.summary:
A majority of companies backed by the Business Development Bank of Canada’s venture capital arm are practising diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI), but those efforts aren’t translating into leadership positions.
The news: BDC Capital released its fifth annual report on DEI and environmental, social, and governance practices on Tuesday. On the DEI side, the report looks at how BDC portfolio companies and supported venture capital general partners (GPs) are engaging with and implementing DEI policies.
From the source: Between 2021 and 2025, BDC surveyed 82 GPs, including 70 BDC-backed GPs and 12 internal teams, and surveyed a sample of its 1,399 eligible portfolio companies. Notably, participation from GPs was spotty, with a non-response rate of 30 percent. Reporting shows more than half of participating GPs have a DEI strategy, and 63 percent have introduced efforts to reduce bias in hiring. 
The context: Among the VC ecosystem, the overall impact of adopting DEI policies and practices is viewed favourably, with 38 percent of respondents saying its impact was positive or very positive; just 1 percent said it had negative impacts. Respondents also cited improved decision-making and innovation (26 percent) and stakeholder expectations (17 percent) as their primary reasons for implementing DEI practices. Both of those metrics were overshadowed, however, by larger percentages of non-responses (30 and 33 percent, respectively).

articles.title: Rockstar dice ‘no’ a una película de GTA, pero no descarta algo como Red Dead Redemption
articles.summary:
Rockstar Games decidió trazar una línea clara entre sus dos franquicias más valiosas. Según reveló The Ankler, el estudio detrás de Grand Theft Auto no tiene intención de llevar la saga a cine o televisión, pese al interés de Hollywood durante años.
La noticia llega en medio del éxito arrollador de GTA 6, que generó cerca de 3.800 millones de dólares al cierre de su primer día en el mercado. Sin embargo, mientras GTA permanece fuera del alcance de productoras y plataformas, Red Dead Redemption sí aparece como una posibilidad concreta de adaptación.
Por qué Rockstar no quiere llevar GTA al cine
De acuerdo con The Ankler, Rockstar Games ha recibido llamados constantes de compañías de entretenimiento interesadas en adaptar Grand Theft Auto a lo largo de los últimos años. A pesar de esa demanda sostenida, el estudio mantiene su negativa.
La franquicia ya genera un nivel de expectativa y atención mediática que, según se desprende del reporte, haría innecesaria cualquier versión televisiva o cinematográfica. Las cifras de ventas de GTA 6 refuerzan ese argumento: se espera que el título termine generando entre tres y cuatro veces lo recaudado por GTA 5, que alcanzó los 1.150 millones de dólares.
El lanzamiento del juego, ocurrido tras una espera de 13 años, coincide además con el momento en que se conoció esta postura del estudio respecto a Hollywood.

articles.title: Santiago, castañero riojano con 44 años de éxito y experiencia: "Antes 8 castañas costaban 100 pesetas, ahora la docena ronda los 4 euros"
articles.summary:
A mediados de los 80, ocho castañas costaban 100 pesetas. Hoy la docena ronda los 4 euros y el oficio del castañero sigue creciendo. Aunque habría que definir ese “creciendo”. Santiago Palacios Cuesta, castañero autónomo y dueño de la SL Coto de Buriz, comenzó en el oficio vendiendo cucuruchos en Logroño, en 1982. Hoy la misma docena, ya decimos, supera los 4 en Cataluña, según ha contado. Y tiene las ofertas de empleo abiertas. Le disputa el puesto a otros castañeros como Mikel Álvarez Menor, de Pamplona, o Paco Pazos, en Pontevedra.
Su oficio parece la tarea de alguien de otro siglo. Y lo es: las castañeras ya eran un arquetipo popular en la Madrid de mediados del siglo XIX. No en vano, aunque la técnica ha cambiado respecto al brasero de toda la vida, asar bien una castaña exige darle muchas vueltas “tener el fuego adecuado y no despistarse”. Además, como dice su propio FAQ, no, las castañas no tienen gluten. Y la buena noticia es que el oficio no están desapareciendo, más bien al contrario.
De un puesto a 76. Santiago Palacios Cuesta tardó 16 años en dar el salto de uno a dos puestos, luego cuatro, ocho, dieciséis y treinta y dos. Hoy El Castañero suma 76 puntos de venta entre Blanes y Castro Urdiales, con paradas también en Tarragona, Cuenca y Zamora. Asa unas 100 toneladas por campaña. Las vende una a una en sus puestos y las suministra a otros castañeros y almacenistas. Lo único que hace la IA son algunos carteles.

5 Lessons from Traitor in the House by Shubha Menon
Explore five powerful lessons from Shubha Menon's Traitor in the House, a memoir about mental health, family trauma, caregiving and resilience.
Traitor in the House: My Bipolar Life by Shubha Menon is a deeply personal memoir about growing up in a family affected by bipolar disorder. Through experiences of childhood trauma, caregiving, denial and eventual diagnosis, Menon explores how untreated mental illness can shape relationships and affect generations.
The book moves beyond the experiences of one individual to examine the emotional realities of families living with mental health challenges. It also explores how understanding, acceptance and self-awareness can help people confront painful experiences.
5 Meaningful lessons from Traitor in the House by Shubha Menon
1. Mental illness should be understood, not judged
One of the most important lessons from the memoir is that mental illness should never be treated as a personal failure or a character flaw. Through her mother's experiences with bipolar disorder, Menon shows how a lack of awareness and understanding can make an already difficult situation more painful for an entire family.
The book highlights the importance of recognising mental health conditions, seeking professional help and replacing judgement with compassion.
Lesson: Understanding someone's struggles is the first step towards treating them with empathy rather than blame.

articles.title: Cyberattaques : l’étude 2026 révèle la vulnérabilité des collectivités locales
articles.summary:

But over the weekend, I started seeing discussions online about a bizarre configuration that can be used to make GTA 6 run at 60 FPS, so to speak. Naturally, I was intrigued.
This configuration involves taking the 30 FPS GTA 6 output from a console like the PlayStation 5, routing it into a capture card connected to a separate PC, and then running 2x frame generation on that video input signal to produce a 60 FPS output. There are several applications that can be used to do this, but the one I've seen discussed most frequently is called Veyra.
Why this sounds like a terrible idea
When I first heard about this configuration, I thought it would be absolutely horrendous. And that's for a few reasons.
First, 30 to 60 FPS frame generation has generally been quite bad in my experience on PC. A game running at a low render rate tends to produce tons of visual artifacts when using frame generation, as the gap between frames is large, leaving the algorithm with more interpolation work to do. The shorter the gap between frames, the better frame generation tends to work, which is why I typically recommend a minimum render rate of 60 FPS.

articles.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
articles.summary:
The Rust team has released Rust 1.100.0, the language's first three-digit stable version, with a release that finally lands the never type after a decade of work. Announced on 12 November 2026, the release also stabilises the core of the custom allocator API, introduces a DropGuard helper, and gives Cargo opt-in dependency cooldowns and warnings for unused dependencies.
The headline is the stabilisation of !, the canonical uninhabited type for computations that never return a value, such as panic!(), return or an endless loop. Although functions have long used it as a return type, naming it elsewhere, for instance writing Result<T, !> to describe an operation that cannot fail, took ten years and five failed stabilisation attempts to land. The release also makes std::convert::Infallible an alias for !, which is what the type was always intended to be, so existing APIs using Infallible now accept ! transparently.
To make that alias work, the team shipped a small breaking change for the 2015, 2018 and 2021 editions, flipping the never-type fallback from () to ! and matching behaviour already introduced in Rust 2024. The release notes describe the impact as largely unnoticeable but warn that more code may be flagged as unreachable. Developers hitting issues on upgrade are advised to update dependencies first, since fixes for widely used crates have already been published.

La demanda contra Luxottica Group, la empresa italiana que fabrica y vende las gafas, se presentó el 23 de noviembre ante el Kammergericht, el tribunal superior de Berlín, según el registro de acciones colectivas de las asociaciones de consumidores. articles.title: Microsoft confirms authentication issues after November updates
articles.summary:
Microsoft has confirmed that customers may experience authentication issues after installing November security updates that address a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability.
Tracked as CVE-2026-118737, this security flaw was found in the Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime and stems from a timing-dependent authentication weakness that unauthenticated attackers can exploit to remotely execute code without user interaction on unpatched systems.
Microsoft says the November security updates represent the first phase of NTLM message-signing improvements, which reduce exposure to relay attacks by ensuring authenticated NTLM sessions always establish a cryptographic session key and negotiate real message signing.
However, as Microsoft explained in an updated support document, the new security improvements introduced to address this vulnerability may also cause authentication failures on patched devices.
"Microsoft is aware of compatibility issues affecting some third-party apps and devices, including authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) solutions, and application packaging solutions that use NTLM authentication," it said.
"This issue can occur when such a proxy device does not correctly implement the NTLM protocol. For example, an affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field."

Energie-Rekord bei Röntgenlasern erzielt: European XFEL in Hamburg übertrifft sich selbst
Erstmals konnten Forscher:innenteams des European XFEL und des DESY an der Forschungsanlage in Hamburg Röntgenlaserblitze mit einer Wellenlänge von etwa 0,04 Nanometern erzeugen und aufrechterhalten. Damit haben sie sich selbst übertroffen und ihren Rekord aus dem Jahr 2020 in den Schatten gestellt.
Laser-Meilenstein: Lichtwellen kleiner als ein Atom
Der European XFEL ist ein Röntgenlaser, der freie Elektronen (FEL, wobei das X für X-ray, also Röntgen steht) statt eines herkömmlichen Lasermediums nutzt. Um die Röntgenblitze zu erzeugen, bringt ein rund 1,7 Kilometer langer Linearbeschleuniger zunächst Elektronenpakete auf nahezu Lichtgeschwindigkeit. Die beschleunigten Elektronenpakete werden dann durch sogenannte Undulatoren auf einen Slalomkurs gezwungen. Das sind tonnenschwere Gerüste, in denen abwechselnd gepolte Magnete sitzen. Bei ihrem Slalomkurs senden die Elektronen Röntgenstrahlung aus; durch die Wechselwirkung der Strahlung mit den Elektronen selbst verstärkt sie sich zu extrem kurzen, intensiven Röntgenblitzen, die für Forschungsexperimente genutzt werden.
Der European XFEL ist eine riesige Maschine – und das nicht nur materiell: Ein Verbund von zwölf Staaten hat diese Anlage für rund 1,5 Milliarden Euro gebaut. Rund 600 Menschen arbeiten fest am XFEL. articles.title: How to Optimize NVFP4 Attention on NVIDIA RTX Blackwell Through Register Recycling
articles.summary:
Attention can be a major bottleneck when serving world foundation models, where long sequences make inference computationally demanding. On NVIDIA Hopper and NVIDIA Blackwell data center GPUs, FlashAttention3 and FlashAttention4 improve attention performance by overlapping matrix multiply-accumulate (MMA) operations through softmax within a thread block.
However, these hardware-specific pipelines cannot be applied directly to the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Series (SM120), which uses a different Tensor Core architecture. For video generation models using BF16 inference, attention remains primarily MMA-bound on NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPUs, while softmax is a major bottleneck in forward attention on Blackwell data center GPUs.
Introduced with NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, NVFP4 offers hardware-accelerated 4-bit matrix multiplication, enabling higher Tensor Core throughput and creating an opportunity to accelerate attention beyond BF16. But sustaining high throughput requires careful coordination of softmax, data movement, and intermediate storage. Dependencies between these stages can leave Tensor Cores idle, limiting how effectively the kernel uses the available compute.
This post explains how to accelerate NVFP4 attention on the SM120 architecture through register recycling and improved scheduling. articles.title: What Happens to Your Returned Gadget? The Hidden Journey of Electronics Returns
articles.summary:
You return a laptop that “just stopped working”. The shop scans the box, hands over a refund and you walk out feeling lighter. Two weeks later, where is that laptop?
Most of us never think about it. But what happens next decides whether the thing gets a second life or ends up in a skip bin. It also shapes the price you pay for new gear, how fair warranty decisions are, and how much e-waste Australia produces. Here’s the journey, step by step.
Why a returned electronic isn’t like a returned jumper
Behind every returned gadget is a process of paperwork, tracking and decisions that most shoppers never see
A jumper goes back on the rack. A laptop doesn’t. Someone has to confirm the serial number, check whether the fault is real, wipe your data, reset the firmware and decide if the battery is safe to ship. Skip any of those and the retailer either resells a dud or throws away a perfectly good machine.
That’s why businesses that sell tech at any scale often bring in dedicated electronics returns management services to handle the messy middle: RMA intake, inspection, functional testing and the call on what happens next. It’s a model that suits retailers, brands and integrators alike, because the work is repetitive, technical and easy to get wrong when it’s squeezed in between everything else a warehouse does.
The trouble is that returns don’t arrive labelled. A “faulty” phone might have a dead battery, a software glitch or a cracked screen from last Tuesday’s drop. Each one leads to…

articles.title: Why Y Combinator is backing fewer African startups
articles.summary:
Four years after African founders made up roughly one in 17 companies in a Y Combinator batch, the continent has become a footnote at Demo Day. The reasons say as much about how YC has changed as about African tech.
In early-2022, Y Combinator’s Winter batch included 24 African startups, 18 of them from Nigeria. For the first time, an African country ranked third in a YC cohort, behind only the United States (US) and India. Lagos founders talked about the accelerator as a rite of passage, and the Paystack exit to Stripe made the path look repeatable.
Indeed, Disrupt Africa wrote articles around that time about the “cult of Y Combinator”, and the rave reviews the programme received from founders that participated in it.
That moment did not last. By Winter 2023 the African count had fallen to three, and Winter 2024 again admitted just three. Africa’s share of a batch had shrunk from about six per cent at the peak to around one per cent by Winter 2024. A search of the YC website for African startups for the 12 batches since then returns the message “sorry, no matching companies found”.
The pullback, however, is not a single decision made in San Francisco. It is the product of three things moving at once – a YC that has changed what it wants, an African funding market that cooled faster than most, and a portfolio record that has made the case for Africa harder to argue.

Einige Fähigkeiten großer KI-Modelle verbessern sich weiterhin exponentiell – aber eben nicht alle. Bei Aufgaben, die Urteilsvermögen erfordern, schneiden sie beispielsweise nicht ganz so gut ab, wie beim Programmieren. Das ist ein Ergebnis eines neuen Berichts der gemeinnützigen Organisation Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR), die an KI-Sicherheit arbeitet.
Doch das ist noch nicht einmal der spannendste Aspekt des Berichts. So liefert METR darin auch eine Aktualisierung einer sehr bekannten Zeithorizont-Grafik der Organisation, die häufig fehlinterpretiert wird. METR bewertet darin die KI-Modelle, indem die Organisation sie eine große Anzahl an Aufgaben ausführen lässt, die jeweils zuvor auch von Menschen erledigt werden konnten. Der Schwierigkeitsgrad jeder Aufgabe wurde daran gemessen, wie lange die menschlichen Tester:innen für deren Erledigung benötigten – und anschließend wurden die Modelle anhand des Zeitumfangs der Aufgaben bewertet, die sie bewältigen konnten. Die entsprechende Grafik zeigte, dass sich KI-Systeme in den vergangenen Jahren rasch verbesserten – alle vier Monate verdoppelte sich die Länge der Aufgaben, die Spitzenmodelle erfolgreich bewältigen konnten.

GTA 6 est un jeu vidéo visuellement sublime. Rockstar Games a bâti un monde ouvert vivant, avec une densité impressionnante et un niveau de détails à tomber à la renverse. Les développeurs ont certes sacrifié la fluidité, avec un affichage limité à 30 images par seconde, mais la prouesse reste immense.
La version PC de GTA 6, qui n’a pas encore été officialisée mais finira par arriver selon la tradition de Rockstar Games, devrait offrir un rendu encore plus incroyable. Comment Rockstar Games a peaufiné les différentes versions de GTA 6

“Attackers sent error-based exploit probes to validate that the server is vulnerable by creating and invoking stored queries,” WatchTowr noted.
WatchTowr has not reported any instances of attackers successfully achieving remote code execution. At the time of writing there do not appear to be any other reports of exploitation attempts.
GeoServer is an open source application for publishing and sharing geospatial data. Government agencies widely use it, and utilities also deploy it. Cybersecurity company Eye Security has identified more than 3,000 internet-accessible GeoServer instances.
CVE-2026-120705 is an XML injection vulnerability that can allow an unauthenticated attacker to obtain sensitive files or conduct server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks. CVE-2026-129243 can enable attackers to bypass access controls and perform operations typically reserved for administrators.
The two security holes are part of a five-bug exploit chain discovered by Rapid7 researcher Jonah Burgess, aka CryptoCat, who reported his findings to GeoServer developers in early August.

articles.title: AI is straining America’s open records systems
articles.summary:
AI is straining America’s open records systems
Startups are mining public data for AI products, while citizens use chatbots to file more requests.
In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer. During morning office hours at the town hall—a wood-frame structure built as a church in 1858—he also fielded public records requests. Recently, he got rather busy.
Panton used to get a request every year or so from a company called SmartProcure for “all purchasing records,” covering everything from road salt to computers to toilet paper. Last year, those requests started coming quarterly. Then different companies began making more specific requests, like records of every purchase related to emergency road flares. These targeted inquiries started coming monthly or more. “I’m happy to answer public records requests from people,” says Rowe, who recently moved into a position at a nearby town. “But answering it for these purposes—it feels like I’m doing unpaid opposition research on the taxpayers’ time.”
Rowe’s experiences are being repeated across the US. While data brokers have mined public records for decades, AI has intensified investors’ interest. Alinea Analytics estimates that Call of Duty HQ's daily player count fell 42% on launch day and barely improved over the next four days. The release also coincided with a shorter disruption outside gaming: Pornhub said its US traffic was 15.5% below normal an hour after GTA 6 went live.
Alinea estimated that Call of Duty HQ had 4.4 million daily active users on launch day, down from an average of 7.5 million across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam. On PlayStation, which Alinea analyst Rhys Elliott identified as Call of Duty's main platform, the decline was 44%. GTA 6 launched only on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, so the overall Call of Duty figure includes a PC storefront where the new game was not available. The combined count does not show how much of the decline came from Steam.
Call of Duty's slow recovery stands out because it had less audience overlap with GTA 6 than Fortnite did. Of the people who played GTA 6 by the end of the launch weekend, 29% had also played Fortnite that month, compared with 16% for Call of Duty HQ and 11% for FC 27. Those figures identify shared audiences, not which game someone stopped playing to make time for GTA 6.

articles.title: Vercel Launched Experimental Board to Coordinate Tasks Across Humans and Coding Agents

Vercel has launched Vercel Board, an experimental, headless message board where people and coding agents coordinate tasks across tools and harnesses. Vercel says Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, eve, fx, Mastra, and LangChain can work on the same board as if they were a single harness.
Each Vercel team gets a default board, named General, organized into channels and threads. Developers and agents read and write through the `vercel board` CLI or the `@vercel/board` JavaScript SDK. A skill, installed with npx skills add vercel/board --skill board, teaches coding agents the CLI. Agents name themselves with --as or BOARD_PROFILE, but still act with the operator's or project's credentials.
A task is a thread whose state the board keeps. A worker claims a ready task, posts updates, and completes or fails it. A claim is a lease of up to five minutes and must be renewed; if it expires, the task returns to the queue. When two workers claim the same task, one succeeds and the other fails with task_claimed. Tasks can declare dependencies, so a review waits until its fix completes while independent work proceeds in parallel. Watchers on a Vercel deployment can run when a reply is posted or a label changes, waking the deployment so no process has to stay running.

articles.title: Todoist confirms 6% of customers' details were stolen in data breach
articles.summary:
Task management app Todoist said on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates. The company said around 6% of its customers were affected and blamed stolen credentials for the breach.
Todoist said the attacker used stolen credentials to access the company’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23. The hacker then changed employee access controls and reached the app’s cloud infrastructure via an employee’s work account.
The hacker downloaded credentials of early Todoist users whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method, but didn’t change any source code, the company said. Todoist said it has blocked the attack path and reset passwords as a mitigation step, as well as disabled the Todoist for Outlook email add-on.
For a small number of people, about 0.001% of its userbase, the hacker also searched through tasks, comments, and attachment names to look for credentials for other services, like API keys and access tokens.
The hacker also pulled Todoist API tokens and Slack integration tokens, and looked for emails, addresses, and attachment file names through the Todoist for Outlook extension if it was connected to accounts and had permission to read emails.
The company said it has sent a notice to those affected and asked them to reset their credentials and change their login details in other places with the same password. The company…

Du hast in den Custom Instructions festgelegt, dass die KI angibt, wie sicher sie sich ist – bei manchen Aufgaben übergeht sie die Vorgabe jedoch einfach. Grund kann die Reihenfolge sein, nach der deine Eingaben priorisiert werden. Diese Erfahrung hat Prompt Engineer Susanne Renate Schneider gemacht.
Bestimmte Vorgaben sind gesetzt
Ganz oben stehen dabei die Sicherheitsregeln der Anbieter wie OpenAI oder Anthropic. Kein Prompt hebelt sie aus, außer gezielte Jailbreaks. Das sind Versuche, durch bestimmte Eingaben Sicherheitsvorkehrungen zu umgehen.
Danach folgen im Job die Vorgaben deines Unternehmens, etwa bei Microsoft Copilot. Auch diese umgehst du nicht per Prompt. Nutzt du KI jedoch privat, fällt diese Ebene weg.
Chat überschreibt mitunter Custom Instructions

Das sind die Eingaben, die du in den Grundeinstellungen deines Nutzeraccounts hinterlegst. Mit ihnen forderst du ein bestimmtes Verhalten der KI dir gegenüber an. articles.summary:
Password management and identity security company 1Password revealed on Wednesday that a hacker stole customer information and proprietary source code. 1Password says customer vaults are not affected.
The company launched an investigation on November 19 after discovering that an employee’s corporate GitHub account may have been compromised.
The attacker used the account to deploy malicious code to backend services and exfiltrate customer records. The compromised customer records include names, email addresses, account identifiers, public cryptographic keys, authentication parameters, account activity times, and non-secret metadata.

articles.title: Wave’s 25 million-user blueprint: How low fees disrupted Francophone West Africa’s mobile money ‘cartels’

As mobile money platform Wave crosses the 25 million active account mark, its Public Policy Lead, Awa Gueye, tells GODFREY GEORGE how the company forced down prices across the WAEMU region—and details the structural and regulatory hurdles that still prevent millions of informal businesses and women from participating fully in the digital economy.
A decade ago, digital payments in Francophone West Africa were still at an early stage, with adoption and the services available gradually expanding. Wave Mobile Money accelerated this development when it launched in the region by introducing a radically lower, flat-fee pricing structure.
The resulting price war forced established telecom-backed operators to slash their own commissions, fundamentally altering the digital payments landscape across the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). MTN MoMo eliminated withdrawal fees in Côte d’Ivoire in 2025, and Orange cut transfer fees to zero ahead of Wave’s launch in Cameroon.
For Awa Gueye, Wave’s Public Policy Lead, the true disruption is not merely in the pricing, but in the shift in consumer psychology.
“The biggest change is in what people expect,” Gueye says. “When someone sends small amounts several times a week, fees decide whether digital payments are part of daily life or reserved for emergencies. Once customers experience a low-cost, simple and reliable service, they expect that standard everywhere.”

Jack Huynh and a veteran overclocker pushed a Radeon RX 9060 XT to 4,837 MHz inside a new Micro Center in Austin. That's reportedly the highest clock speed any graphics chip has ever reached.
Huynh had come to town to celebrate the store's opening with local gamers and PC builders. On November 15, two days after the grand opening, he joined Bill "Sampson" Alverson and AMD's in-house overclocking team for a liquid-nitrogen session. He posted about it on X only this Tuesday, along with a video he says captures the exact moment the record fell.
On paper, the RX 9060 XT's boost clock tops out at 3,130 MHz, so the run pushed the chip roughly 55% past AMD's own spec. It's also nearly double the 2,530 MHz that AMD expects the card to hold in a typical game.
This is actually the third time this year that an RX 9060 XT has claimed a new high. AMD and overclocker Splave first pushed one to 4,769 MHz at the company's Markham office back in February. Then in June, Sampson and a South Korean overclocker called SoonHo edged past that with 4,789 MHz. Huynh's run tops their mark by just 48 MHz.

JetBrains has launched a new variant of its open source coding model, one designed to tackle quick code edits, tool calls and all the smaller tasks that AI coding agents perform in the course of solving bigger problems.
Mellum2.1 Instruct, as it’s called, is the latest installment in JetBrains’ in-house coding model lineup. The original Mellum, which debuted back in 2024, was a proprietary model built specifically for low-latency code completion in JetBrains’ IDEs.

"We've installed 3 separate versions of 365 on this device, but no matter how we try to get into a 365 app we get stuck on this white screen. I've launched applications in safe mode as well without any luck," one user said.
The company confirmed in a support document updated Monday that a blank dialog box prevented customers from opening Microsoft 365 Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, and Access apps.

In the current memory-hungry, AI-driven landscape, severe supply constraints have driven prices to all-time highs, even when supply is available. With demand continuing to grow and supply unlikely to catch up for at least the next two years, if not longer, and no significant breakthroughs in memory technology on the horizon, the industry is looking for ways to use available memory more efficiently. The good news is that AMD might have just found a solution.
Solving the memory crisis
MEXT, a software company that AMD worked with and later acquired, found that much of the RAM in any given system is often wasted, with DRAM often overprovisioned, stranded, and underused. When analyzing RAM usage, MEXT found that 50% to 80% of memory pages in RAM are stale and have not been accessed by compute resources for more than five minutes. Those pages, known as cold pages, are kept there just in case they are needed again. Addressing this inefficiency is the basis of the solution AMD announced earlier this month.
At the recent AMD In Depth 2026 event in Las Vegas, the company announced AMD MEXT, a software solution designed to make better use of RAM by leveraging flash storage as a “parking lot” for memory pages until they are needed and brought back into RAM. This solution requires no hardware or software modifications to existing deployments and will be available alongside AMD EPYC CPUs.

How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
Rising electricity demand is locking in fossil-fuel generation.
In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right.
Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence.
Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on in his story have expanded, and its power needs have too. The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10. And as I wrote in a new story this week, data center developers are now looking beyond the grid and planning to build their own off-grid gas power plants. How did we get here?
If you want to understand the future of the grid, one way to do it is by looking at interconnection queues—lists of power plants that have requested a connection to the system. In recent years these queues have been dominated by renewables like wind and solar power, which are generally the cheapest way to build new energy capacity today.

Schweres Schwarzes Loch in der Frühzeit des Universums
