Im Zentrum von „Dún Aonghasa“ sitzt den Berechnungen zufolge ein Schwarzes Loch mit rund 360 Millionen Sonnenmassen. Es übertrifft das Schwarze Loch im Milchstraßenzentrum um das 90-Fache – zu einer Zeit, als der Kosmos unter fünf Prozent seines heutigen Alters lag.
Damit blickt Euclid rund 39 Millionen Jahre weiter zurück als beim bisherigen Rekordquasar vom Juli 2026, den Astronom:innen um die niederländische Universität Leiden vorstellten. Die neue Untersuchung entstand maßgeblich am Max-Planck-Institut für Astronomie in Heidelberg. Erstautor Julien Wolf wechselte inzwischen zur Europäischen Südsternwarte in Garching bei München.

OpenAI claims to have solved a problem that has occupied theoretical computer scientists since 1969. In a preprint published Tuesday on GitHub, the company presents a lower bound for the exponent of square matrix multiplication that matches the upper bound of 2.25 it reported in October.
OpenAI claims to have solved a problem that has occupied theoretical computer scientists since 1969.
If the proof holds, developers working on numerical libraries and AI infrastructure will know where the mathematical limit lies and can focus on other ways to improve performance.
The paper is one of nine manuscripts OpenAI released Tuesday, seven of which apply a new geometric theory of tensors to problems in arithmetic complexity and combinatorics.
Bounding the exponent at 2.25
In 1969, Volker Strassen showed that two n × n matrices could be multiplied with an arithmetic exponent below three, prompting researchers to see how close they could get to two.

Amini, a startup building sovereign AI infrastructure for governments in the Global South, has released Soma-1X Lite, an open-weight AI model designed to convert paper-based records into machine-readable data, targeting African countries that hold most public records in physical archives.
The company says the two-billion-parameter model can process about 15,000 pages per hour at an estimated graphics processing unit (GPU) computing cost of $0.22 per 1,000 pages. Clinton Oduor, Amini’s Head of Data Science, told TechCabal that, in an evaluation of 435 document pages across ten African languages, including Yoruba, Hausa, Swahili and Wolof, the model recorded an average character error rate of 2.9%—the lowest among the five models tested.
It can run on a GPU-equipped workstation without a dedicated data centre, or on a central processing unit (CPU), albeit slower. The model can also process documents offline, without relying on external AI services, according to Oduor.
The release comes as African governments seek to make their public records accessible, many of which remain in paper archives. Even where government information has been digitised, making it usable by digital systems remains a challenge. A 2019 Africa Open Data Index by Open Knowledge International, which assessed 420 government datasets across 30 African countries, found that only 14.5% were available in machine-readable formats.

articles.title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability
articles.summary:
DoorDash has rebuilt its real-time dispatch platform to handle growing delivery demand, replacing a monolithic optimization engine with a distributed architecture that separates coordination from computation. The redesign delivers 10 times higher throughput and more than 99.99% availability during peak periods, while enabling the company to run machine learning and reinforcement learning models within dispatch workflows.
The previous dispatch engine tightly coupled business logic, logistics state management, and computationally intensive routing algorithms. As delivery volume increased, its optimization workload became increasingly difficult to process within the time available for dispatch decisions. The underlying algorithms had roughly quadratic time complexity, and during peak periods, demand approached four times the system's processing capacity. The engine consequently relied on fallback heuristics and sometimes made assignment decisions using incomplete information.
As the DoorDash engineering team explained:
The fatal bottleneck wasn't just raw machine capacity; it was the speed of reality.
Rather than address the bottleneck through conventional horizontal scaling, DoorDash redesigned the execution model around two independently scalable tiers. The engineering team described the motivation:
To scale into the future, the system didn't just need more capacity; it demanded a fundamentally new execution model.

articles.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
articles.summary:
AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  York University
- Summary:
  AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A new study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.
For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.
But the new findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?

articles.title: InfraTrust warns of exploited supply chain flaws in network appliances
articles.summary:
Eclypsium's November InfraTrust report warns that most infrastructure security advisories addressing exploited vulnerabilities over the past month involve flaws in third-party software bundled into products rather than code developed by the vendors themselves.
The November InfraTrust Pulse report tracks 373 new security advisories published by 23 infrastructure vendors between October 15 and November 19, covering 3,880 vulnerabilities.
Of these advisories, 98 were rated critical, and 38 contained vulnerabilities listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
However, 33 of those 38 advisories fixed exploited flaws in bundled software components, primarily PHP, Node.js, and OpenSSH.
These vulnerabilities pose additional risks for enterprises, as even after a software developer releases a security fix, organizations must wait for infrastructure vendors to incorporate it into their products.
"Your exposure to exploited flaws depends on how quickly each vendor rebuilds its products after an upstream fix ships," the report reads.
An example of this is the two PHP vulnerabilities known as PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) highlighted in last month's InfraTrust report, which are now being exploited in attacks against Palo Alto Networks and Check Point firewalls.
In both cases, threat actors chained the PHP vulnerabilities with other flaws to gain root access to compromised devices, with Check Point reporting destructive attacks that deployed data-wipin…

articles.title: Según los psicólogos, las personas que crecieron en los años 80 y 90 han desarrollado la falacia de la llegada por culpa de los finales felices
articles.summary:
En las películas de Disney (y también en las comedias románticas) puede haber un momento en que los protagonistas obtienen lo que han estado persiguiendo a lo largo de toda la película. Por ejemplo, pueden conseguir el ascenso que querían o incluso casarse con la persona de sus sueños. El famoso “y fueron felices para siempre” resume ese tipo de final. Este tipo de finales aparece en películas de los 80 y 90. También sirve para ilustrar esta expectativa.
El experto en psicología positiva Tal Ben-Shahar utiliza este ejemplo para ilustrar la llamada falacia de la llegada. Tenemos la sensación de que cuando alcancemos nuestro objetivo vamos a ser felices. Pero damos por hecho que la felicidad del día que conseguimos el objetivo va a durar. Las fuentes no muestran evidencia de que ver estas películas haya generado esta expectativa en las personas que crecieron en esos decenios.
Qué pasa después de conseguir un objetivo
Por un lado, el efecto de alegría que genera conseguir un objetivo puede ir decayendo con el tiempo. Kennon Sheldon y Sonja Lyubomirsky han estudiado esto. Se trata de la llamada adaptación hedónica. En su estudio mostraron que las emociones placenteras que experimentaban los participantes al recordar un cambio positivo eran, en promedio, menos intensas en la segunda medición. Por otro lado, tras un cambio positivo podemos desarrollar nuevas aspiraciones. El ascenso puede seguir siendo una buena noticia (tras pasar la euforia del primer día).

articles.title: Amazon’s cumulative ecommerce exports from India reach $27B
articles.summary:
Amazon’s cumulative ecommerce exports from India reach $27B
The milestone marks continued progress towards Amazon’s goal of enabling $80 billion in cumulative e-commerce exports from India by 2030, the company said.
Ecommerce major Amazon on Wednesday said it has reached $27 billion in cumulative ecommerce exports from India through its Amazon Global Selling programme, with the number of exporters on the platform rising 20% in a year to 2.4 lakh.
The milestone marks continued progress towards Amazon’s goal of enabling $80 billion in cumulative ecommerce exports from India by 2030, the company said in a statement.
Launched in 2015, the programme has registered over 2.4 lakh exporters, who have sold more than one billion 'Made-in-India' products to customers across Amazon's global marketplaces.
The increase in cumulative exports was $7 billion this year, the same as last year, when it rose from $13 billion at the end of 2024 to $20 billion in October 2025.
"India has the potential to become a global powerhouse for consumer exports, and e-commerce is helping turn that ambition into reality, creating opportunities for every Indian seller to become a global exporter. We see tremendous opportunity in sectors like textiles, where India's manufacturing strengths, craftsmanship and entrepreneurial talent can translate into globally recognised brands," said Srinidhi Kalvapudi, Head of Amazon Global Selling in India.

articles.title: Kenya’s Cloud9 acquires Canadian money services business Monix Pay
articles.summary:
Kenyan digital bank Cloud9, which enables cross-border payments and borderless banking for African consumers and businesses, has acquired Canadian money services business Monix Pay to expand into North America.
Disrupt Africa reported in October 2025 on the launch of Cloud9, a digital bank enabling instant global payments, borderless banking and modern financial tools for a new generation of African consumers and businesses.
The startup recently secured an undisclosed investment from crypto and fintech accelerator Alliance, taking total funding to date to US$1 million, and it has now acquired Monix Pay, a Canadian money services business registered with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), the country’s financial intelligence and anti-money-laundering regulator.
The deal sees Cloud9 expand into North America for the first time, and means it is now registered to provide foreign exchange (FX) services, money transfers, general payment services, and virtual currency and digital asset transactions. It is a key step in the startup’s long-term plan to own the regulated infrastructure its customers depend on, rather than fully renting it from intermediaries.

articles.title: Kosmisches Pech für einen Stern – was passiert, wenn er ein Schwarzes Loch verschluckt?
articles.summary:
MIT-Studie: Können atomgroße Schwarze Löcher ganze Sterne von innen zerstören?
Forscher:innen um den Physiker Ore Gottlieb vom Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in Cambridge haben dieses Szenario durchgerechnet. Atomgroße Schwarze Löcher könnten demnach Sterne von innen zerstören, wie in einer im Fachjournal „The Astrophysical Journal“ veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist.
Gemeint sind sogenannte primordiale Schwarze Löcher, die theoretisch im ersten Sekundenbruchteil nach dem Urknall aus dichter Materie entstanden sein könnten. Anders als frühe große Schwarze Löcher im jungen Kosmos wären solche hypothetischen Objekte höchstens so groß wie ein einzelnes Atom, aber so schwer wie ein Asteroid.
Noch leichtere Exemplare hätten sich über Jahrmilliarden durch quantenmechanische Teilchenabstrahlung, die sogenannte Hawking-Strahlung, längst vollständig aufgelöst. Zwischen 100 Milliarden und 100 Billiarden Tonnen Masse bleibt dagegen eine Beobachtungslücke, in der solche Objekte die Dunkle Materie bilden könnten.
Schwerkraft von Planeten lenkt kleine Schwarze Löcher in fremde Sterne
Trifft ein solches Mini-Schwarzes-Loch im Alleingang auf einen Stern, bremst das dichte Sterngas den Eindringling wegen seiner geringen Masse kaum ab. Das Objekt durchquert den Stern einmalig mit hoher Geschwindigkeit und fliegt anschließend weiter durch den freien Weltraum.

articles.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
articles.summary:
WhatsApp on Wednesday started rolling out a much-sought-after feature: the ability to schedule messages in both individual and group chats.
The feature is rolling out globally to all users across iOS and Android. Once it becomes available, you can type a message and long-press the send button to schedule it. You can choose to send a message anywhere between 10 minutes and 14 days later.
Users will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed. It’s not clear if there is a way to edit the schedule of a message.
Notably, scheduled messages will be sent even if your phone is off or outside network coverage. You can schedule messages containing text, photos, and videos.
The feature could prove useful for wishing someone a happy birthday on time or chatting with people across time zones. Businesses may also find it easier to schedule texts and updates to their customers, and people who use the app to coordinate work will likely find themselves using scheduled texts to update their teams.
WhatsApp rivals like Telegram and Signal have had the ability to schedule messages for a while now, so the Meta-owned chat app is late in rolling it out.

articles.title: BepiColombo has finally reached Mercury after an eight-year trip
articles.summary:
The big picture: BepiColombo has entered orbit around Mercury after an eight-year flight that used solar-powered electric engines and repeated planetary flybys to slow the spacecraft down. The European Space Agency said BepiColombo entered Mercury's orbit with both probes still attached. The probes will separate and take up different orbits, putting one close to the surface and sending the other much farther out to measure how Mercury's magnetic field interacts with the solar wind.
Getting to Mercury meant shedding speed, not just covering distance. After its launch in October 2018, BepiColombo had to move closer to the Sun without picking up so much speed that it overshot the planet. "Energetically, it takes more energy to go to Mercury than to go to the outer Solar System," Emma Bunce, a University of Leicester plasma physicist and one of the mission's lead scientists, told Nature.
To limit the amount of propellant it needed to carry, BepiColombo relied mainly on solar-powered electric propulsion rather than conventional thrusters. The electric propulsion system did not work entirely as planned, delaying the mission by 11 months.
The spacecraft also used gravity assists from Earth, the Moon, Venus, and Mercury over nine circuits around the Sun. Mercury itself helped slow the spacecraft before it entered orbit: BepiColombo flew past the planet six times, capturing its first close-up images of Mercury during the initial flyby in 2021.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.summary:
AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  University of Plymouth
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.
- Share:
Bladder cancer kills approximately 220,000 people worldwide each year, yet recognizing the disease early can be difficult. Its symptoms can resemble those of far less serious conditions, including kidney stones, allowing warning signs to go unnoticed.
Researchers at the University of Plymouth have now developed an artificial intelligence system that could help doctors identify people at risk of bladder cancer years before they receive a diagnosis. In some patients, the technology detected subtle warning signals dating back as far as five years.
The new approach uses AI to examine electronic health records, searching for combinations of symptoms, medical conditions, risk factors, and healthcare activity that might otherwise be overlooked. By recognizing these patterns, researchers hope to make bladder cancer screening more accurate and help doctors find the disease when treatment is most likely to succeed.

Silicon Valley tiene un problema de culto a la personalidad
articles.summary:
Cuando Jensen Huang regresó a las oficinas de Nvidia tras ser restituido como CEO, se topó con una multitud aguardando al otro lado de la puerta. Centenares de ojos le miraban con atención. En otras circunstancias, uno pensaría que el veredicto de la muchedumbre sería severo: al fin y al cabo, Huang había reconocido varias aventuras extramatrimoniales, había tenido contacto con una potencial espía china y había puesto en grave riesgo la salud financiera de la empresa más valiosa del planeta.
En su lugar se llevó una ovación.
Huang se había comportado de forma irresponsable. Su propia restitución, mediada por la Casa Blanca y en contra de la voluntad inicial de la junta de accionistas, revestía tonos amorales. Nada de esto parecía importarle a los empleados de Nvidia. Entre aplausos, Huang manifestó su arrepentimiento y su felicidad por volver a la normalidad. Un desliz de juventud. Peccata minuta. Quiénes somos nosotros, simples mortales, para enjuiciar a nuestro becerro de oro.
La ovación a Huang apunta a un problema más profundo: Silicon Valley se ha entregado al culto a la personalidad. En ninguna otra empresa se manifiesta de forma tan clara como en Anthropic: cuando una delegación de la compañía viajó al Vaticano para discutir sobre Claude, lo hizo abierta a la posibilidad de que hubiera desarrollado alma; cuando un periodista del New York Times pasó un año dentro de la empresa, se topó con una cultura laboral ensimismada y convencida de su misión existencial.

articles.title: Why Nigerian companies are investing in Kenya
articles.summary:
Before Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, settled on Lamu, a historic town on Kenya’s coast, for his second major refinery, he considered Tanga, on the Tanzanian coast. In July, his group told Reuters that infrastructure, logistics, and market access tipped the decision in Kenya’s favour.
Then, in October, Greenview Oil Trading, an investment vehicle linked to Dangote, paid about KES 42.5 billion ($30.7 million) for almost a quarter of Kenya Pipeline Company (KPC). Both investments address different parts of the same problem. A refinery capable of processing 700,000 barrels a day needs somewhere to send the fuel. Kenya already has a network that takes it inland from the coast and into several neighbouring markets, including Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and South Sudan.
The Kenyan appeal to Nigerian firms looking for growth is showing up in very different parts of Kenya’s economy.
On November 16, Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) disclosed it had acquired 10% of the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). In March, Nigerian fintech Moniepoint acquired a controlling stake in Sumac Microfinance Bank. Access Bank, which entered Kenya six years ago by acquiring Transnational Bank, is now folding that operation into National Bank of Kenya (NBK).
In each of these multimillion-dollar transactions, each buyer found an entity and a market already in place that would be expensive or slow to build from scratch.

articles.title: "Ni siquiera sé por qué todavía tenemos Phone Dialer": un directivo de Microsoft admite que Windows 11 aún incluye una app de Windows 95 para módems que nadie usa
articles.summary:
Windows 11 es la versión más moderna del sistema operativo de Microsoft, pero sigue incluyendo varias herramientas que ya cuentan con varias décadas a sus espaldas. Es el caso del Marcador de teléfono, una aplicación de la época de Windows 95 que servía para hacer llamadas de voz a través del módem, algo que ni siquiera en Microsoft parecen tener claro por qué sigue ahí. Y un ejemplo son las palabras de Brandon LeBlanc, director de comunicación de Windows, que respondió en X a un usuario diciendo: “ni siquiera sé por qué todavía tenemos Phone Dialer, estaba pensado para una época en la que los PC tenían módems”.
Una reliquia a un Win+R de distancia. Cualquier persona puede probar esta herramienta abriendo la función de Ejecutar con Win+R, escribiendo dialer y pulsando Enter para abrirla. Eso sí, cuando lo hagas te aparecerá un mensaje diciéndote que no encuentra ningún módem ni dispositivo de teléfono con el que hacer llamadas de voz, o sea que tampoco lo puedes utilizar..
Y es que el programa nació para un tipo de ordenador que prácticamente ha desaparecido. En la época de Windows 95 muchos equipos tenían un módem, interno o externo, conectado con un cable a la toma del teléfono fijo, y el Marcador era la manera de utilizar el ordenador para hacer llamadas de voz, con la posibilidad de guardar números de marcación rápida. articles.title: Falla crítica en VMware permite entrar sin contraseña al sistema que controla los servidores de empresas
articles.summary:
Broadcom, la empresa propietaria de VMware, publicó parches para corregir una falla crítica en vCenter, el programa con el que muchas empresas administran sus servidores virtuales. El error permite que un atacante con acceso a la red entre al sistema sin credenciales.
La compañía le asignó 9,8 puntos sobre 10 en la escala de gravedad CVSS, la más alta de su categoría crítica. La firma de seguridad Rapid7, que analizó el aviso, explicó que el problema está en el servicio de directorio de vCenter, el componente que guarda las cuentas y los permisos de acceso.
Según Rapid7, quien alcance ese servicio por la red puede acceder al sistema sin autenticarse. Para el atacante, el resultado equivale a tener las llaves de la sala de control: vCenter gestiona los servidores y las máquinas virtuales de una organización.
Broadcom no ofrece una solución alternativa para esta falla: la única salida es instalar la actualización. Las preguntas frecuentes que la compañía publicó junto al aviso dicen que no hay soluciones provisionales para estas vulnerabilidades, y que los parches de vCenter no admiten el método de actualización rápida.
Una prueba de ataque ya es pública
Rapid7 señaló que existe una prueba de concepto pública, es decir, un código que demuestra cómo explotar el error. La firma afirmó que la validó y que logró saltarse la autenticación. Hasta la publicación de su análisis, el 25 de noviembre, no había reportes de ataques reales con esta falla.

Le principe est simple : on peut rédiger un message maintenant et choisir son jour et son heure d’envoi. Un usage régulièrement demandé pour souhaiter un anniversaire à minuit sans rester éveillé, relancer un collègue le lundi matin ou écrire à un proche installé dans un autre fuseau horaire.

articles.title: SaaS Sprawl Is Becoming a Project Delivery Problem: How Distributed Teams Keep Work Connected
articles.summary:
For many organisations, adopting another cloud application no longer feels like a technology decision. A new communication platform solves one problem, a specialist tool improves another workflow, a shared drive handles documents, spreadsheets fill reporting gaps and a separate system tracks resources or budgets.
Each addition can be perfectly rational. The difficulty appears later, when the work itself has to move across all of them. A project manager may receive an important decision in chat, update a deadline in a task tool, confirm resource availability in a spreadsheet and then recreate the same situation in a management report. Nothing is necessarily missing, yet the overall picture becomes harder to trust.
This is the operational side of SaaS sprawl. The issue is not simply that a business pays for too many subscriptions. It is that project context becomes distributed across tools at the same time as the teams doing the work become distributed across locations. Hybrid and international teams are particularly exposed because informal coordination is already more difficult. When colleagues cannot resolve an ambiguity by turning to the person sitting next to them, every missing decision, outdated status or unclear handoff has more opportunity to become a delay.
More tools can create less visibility
Modern work encourages specialised software. Communication tools are designed for fast conversation, document platforms for collaboration, CRM systems for customer activity and…

articles.title: « Code rouge » : après la panne historique d’Outlook, Microsoft déclenche l’alerte maximale
articles.summary:
Microsoft tire la sonnette d’alarme. Nos confrères de Reuters révèlent que le géant de Redmond a déclenché un « code rouge » à la suite de la panne historique de ses services. Du 12 au 13 novembre dernier, Outlook, Teams, Copilot, et SharePoint étaient en effet inaccessibles dans le monde. La panne a touché des gouvernements de l’Australie au Japon en passant par les États-Unis, retardé des sociétés de trading et perturbé les communications de compagnies aériennes. En France, des collectivités et une agence régionale de santé se sont retrouvées sans messagerie pendant une journée complète. Incapable de réagir et de corriger le problème pendant des heures, Microsoft a fini par pointer du doigt un correctif défectueux, déployé en juillet dernier.
Chez Microsoft, le code rouge est le niveau d’alerte le plus grave et le plus urgent. Réservée aux crises critiques, l’alerte s’accompagne d’une mobilisation exceptionnelle des équipes de Microsoft. En clair, celles-ci doivent mettre de côté tous leurs autres projets pour se consacrer au problème unique identifié par les responsables de Microsoft.
« Code rouge signifie qu’il s’agit du travail le plus prioritaire pour notre équipe », écrit Jason Henderson, président de Microsoft 365 Core, la division qui gère les services de base de Microsoft 365, dans un mémo interne intercepté par Reuters.

articles.title: More Pentests Without More Pentesters: Where AI Safely Helps
articles.summary:
Demand for penetration testing keeps rising, be it due to DORA threat-led testing, NIS2, or customer security questionnaires. However, supply often cannot keep up.
Experienced testers are scarce, take months to hire and train, and every one of them spends part of each engagement on work that is not testing. For a company that sells hours, that unbillable part is the margin.
This article shows how to measure it, which parts AI can take over, and how to do that without sending client vulnerabilities to someone else's servers.
Step 1: Measure where an engagement's hours go
Most companies track billable testing time and lack a number for the rest. If you tag the last ten engagements by phase, the picture usually changes:
| Phase | What to count | Share of hours | 
|---|---|---|
| Scoping and kickoff | Calls, scope documents, access setup | 8% | 
| Testing | Recon, exploitation, validation | 50% | 
| Documentation | Writing findings, screenshots, formatting | 22% | 
| Review | Senior QA, rework, client comments | 8% | 
| Delivery and retest | Report handover, status questions, retest | 12% | 
Two ratios matter: documentation plus review as a share of testing time, and calendar days from last testing day to report delivery. The first sums up to the hidden cost, but only the second is what clients feel.

articles.title: Samsung Doubles Down on V9 NAND in China

Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Samsung Doubles Down on V9 NAND in China
Samsung is reportedly planning to increase its NAND production capacity in China, but it's unfortunately not the kind of NAND flash that will benefit regular consumers directly. According to Seoul Economic Daily, citing industry sources, Samsung plans to make roughly five times as much V9 NAND flash at its second fab in Xi'an, China, by the end of 2027. Sources tell SED that the X2 fab currently produces about 10,000 300 mm wafers of the 286-layer V9 NAND per month, and the plan is to raise that figure to around 50,000. This extra output is, to the surprise of no one, aimed at enterprise SSDs for AI data centers. It's interesting that this report has surfaced when NAND spot prices have already started falling.
As for the exact plans, the report says that Samsung will build an electroplating line in X2's empty cleanroom space, move equipment in around February 2027, and finish the conversion by November 2027. Additionally, 20% to 30% of the fab's existing V6 line will also be switched to V9. Overall, this looks like a plan to mostly shift to denser NAND inside an existing fab, rather than a brand-new factory expansion. Samsung has previously denied claims of expanding production capacity, so this might be more of a reshuffle. articles.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
articles.summary:
About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics.
LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online.
The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI.
They asked other physicists for some of their private gems—minor but real findings they’d never gotten around to cleaning up for public display. They were asking for real work, problems that take humans at the top of the field about a day to solve.

articles.title: How PCB Design Affects Battery Life in Smart Home Devices
articles.summary:
Smart home devices are becoming part of everyday life. From wireless door sensors and smart locks to temperature monitors and security systems, many connected devices promise months or even years of operation without needing a battery replacement.
Yet battery life can vary significantly between products that appear to perform similar functions.
While battery capacity is an obvious factor, the electronics inside a device play an equally important role. Power management, wireless communication, component selection, and printed circuit board (PCB) design all influence how efficiently a smart device uses energy.
Understanding these factors helps explain why some devices last longer than others.
1. The Hidden Power Consumption Inside Smart Devices
A smart home sensor may appear inactive for most of the day, but its internal electronics are rarely completely switched off.
Even when the device is not actively collecting or transmitting data, certain components may continue drawing small amounts of current.
Typical power consumers include:
- Microcontrollers responsible for processing sensor information
- Wireless communication chips
- Voltage regulators and power management circuits
- Sensors and monitoring components
- Status indicators and supporting circuitry
The total energy consumption depends on both how much current these components draw and how long they remain active.

Für die Erhebung werteten die Wissenschaftler:innen in drei zeitversetzten Befragungen Angaben von insgesamt 747 Arbeitnehmer:innen und 257 Führungskräften aus. „Selbst gute Führungskräfte können bei manchen Mitarbeiter:innen unbeabsichtigt Druck erzeugen“, sagt Erstautorin Lin Xiao Chu in einer Mitteilung.
Warum eine Fassade im Job mehr belastet als hohe Eigenansprüche
Ausschlaggebend ist dabei weniger der innere Anspruch eines Menschen, für sich selbst möglichst fehlerfreie Arbeit abzuliefern. Gefährdet sind laut der Untersuchung vor allem Mitarbeiter:innen, die vor wichtigen Beurteiler:innen eine makellose Fassade aufbauen und ihren Eindruck gezielt steuern wollen.
Solche Teammitglieder stellen Erfolge heraus, verschweigen Schwächen oder verbergen Fehler, weil sie Unverwundbarkeit im Berufsalltag mit Kompetenz verwechseln. articles.title: A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a new way to cause chaos
articles.summary:
One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history: cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food.
Hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command.
The group, which often goes by the online persona CyberAv3ngers, has a history of targeting critical infrastructure. In 2023 and 2024, it hacked Israeli-made industrial control devices inside water, manufacturing, and transportation systems across several US states. Operational disruption was minimal, but the attackers left a message each time: “Every equipment ‘made in Israel’ is CyberAv3ngers legal target.”
State-backed Iranian hackers have rarely targeted Europe in this way, however. October’s hacks, experts say, mark an escalation in the Islamic republic’s cyber warfare strateg…

L’intrus s’en était servi pour copier du code source, accéder à la chaîne de déploiement et envoyer vers les serveurs de 1Password un code malveillant qui lui a permis de récupérer des informations sur certains clients.
Six jours plus tard, l’entreprise a détaillé l’incident dans un article de blog, en insistant sur un point : « les coffres des clients n’ont pas été affectés ».
Quelles données ont été volées
Selon l’entreprise, les fiches copiées contiennent les noms et adresses mail de connexion, les identifiants de compte, les dates de création et de dernière connexion, ainsi que des métadonnées techniques que 1Password juge sans danger.
Certaines de ces fiches contiennent également des jetons présents dans les liens envoyés par mail lors d’une invitation ou d’une récupération de compte. Le communiqué précise que seul un petit nombre d’utilisateurs avaient une telle procédure en cours, et que ceux-ci ont été prévenus individuellement.
Ces jetons ne permettent pas à eux seuls de prendre le contrôle d’un compte, puisqu’il faut aussi une connexion SSO ou un code envoyé par mail. Par précaution, l’entreprise a remplacé ce code à six chiffres par dix caractères alphanumériques.

La compañía confirmó que días atrás sufrió el acceso sin autorización a sus servidores y el robo de algunos datos de los usuarios. Pese a lo malo del incidente, la buena noticia es que las bóvedas y las contraseñas guardadas no se han visto impactadas.
De acuerdo con 1Password, el actor malicioso detrás del ataque pudo copiar parte de la información perteneciente a un grupo reducido de usuarios. De momento, la empresa no ha revelado un número preciso de clientes impactados por esta situación. Lo que sí ha mencionado es que en ninguno de los casos se ha vulnerado las contraseñas o claves secretas almacenadas en el servicio.
Así las cosas, 1Password está llevando calma a quienes utilizan su plataforma para gestionar las contraseñas de sus servicios en línea. Desde la firma aseguran que no es necesario realizar cambios en las cuentas de usuarios, ni nada por el estilo. Además, tanto las apps como los sistemas de la plataforma no han dejado de funcionar en ningún momento.
Cómo se produjo el hackeo a 1Password y qué datos robaron
Según reveló 1Password, el hackeo se produjo luego de que un atacante obtuvo acceso al GitHub de la compañía tras robar las credenciales de uno de los empleados. Esto permitió acceder introducir código malicioso en los sistemas de la plataforma y exfiltrar lo que se ha catalogado como "datos administrativos" vinculados con los clientes.

articles.title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
articles.summary:
Mock Service Worker, the API mocking library maintained by Artem Zakharchenko, has released version 3.0, nearly three years after the Fetch-based v2.0 rewrite. The release ships as ESM-only, completes the library's GraphQL story with subscription support, and introduces a socket-based interception algorithm in Node.js that Zakharchenko describes as going as deep into the runtime as JavaScript will allow without recompiling Node.
The headline breaking change is that MSW is now distributed natively as ECMAScript Modules only, with support for Node.js v18 and v20 dropped in favour of v22, v24, and v26. TypeScript 5.9 is now the minimum supported version. Several transitive dependencies have been removed, including graphql (now a proper optional peer), path-to-regexp, picocolors, and statuses. The result is a library tarball that drops from 416KB to 234KB, with type definitions shrinking by half, from 190KB to 90KB.
Alongside ESM, v3.0 introduces granular entrypoints that replace the single msw import with designated paths for each protocol:
import { http } from 'msw/http'
import { graphql } from 'msw/graphql'
import { sse } from 'msw/sse'
import { ws } from 'msw/ws'
GraphQL subscription support, a long-standing community request on the project's tracker, lands in this release. articles.title: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach
articles.summary:
1Password has disclosed a data breach after an employee's corporate GitHub account was hacked and used to deploy malicious code to the company's backend services to steal customer data.
The company says customer password vaults and the encryption keys protecting them were not compromised in the attack.
In a security incident disclosure published today, 1Password says it began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting indications that an employee's GitHub account had been compromised.
The attacker used the account to access private source code repositories and inject malicious code into backend services that downloaded customer account records.
The stolen data includes:
- Customer names and email addresses
- Account and user IDs
- Account creation and last sign-in timestamps
- Public cryptographic keys
- Secure Remote Password (SRP) protocol parameters

articles.title: Capcom Axes Live Service Game "Exoprimal" After Just 3 Years

Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Capcom Axes Live Service Game "Exoprimal" After Just 3 Years
It seems as though Sony isn't the only gaming stalwart struggling to make sense of a changing live-service gaming landscape. Exoprimal launched on Steam in July 2023 with what ought to be a convincing concept: mech suits versus dinosaurs; and it looked like Capcom had big plans for the game. However, it appears as though a compelling gameplay concept just isn't enough in a world flooded with live-service games, as the online PvP shooter failed to even crack 5,000 concurrent players on Steam. 
Now, just over three years since its launch, Capcom has announced that it will be shutting down Exoprimal for good in September 2027. Capcom has not provided a reason for the game shutting down, but it's safe to assume the low player retention is to blame. As of November 24, 2026, Exoprimal players will no longer be able to buy the Survival Pass Premium battle pass tiers. The game itself will be delisted on March 30, 2027, and the servers will shut down on September 29, 2027. There does not appear to be a post-service plan to keep the game alive at all—unlike the recently discontinued Splitgate: Arena Reloaded and Empulse, which both received a final patch allowing peer-to-peer hosting.

These are important questions, and they will continue to matter. But there is another question that deserves equal attention: what does the customer actually get from that flight?
A drone may spend several hours monitoring an area and return with a large volume of footage. Yet, if the operator has to spend several more hours reviewing that footage to identify something important, much of the benefit is lost. The real value lies not simply in collecting information, but in making sense of it and using it at the right time.
I believe this is where the next phase of the drone industry will take shape.
The value does not end when the drone lands
As drones become more widely used across defence, infrastructure, mapping, and homeland security, customer expectations are changing. Buying a drone is increasingly becoming the beginning of a larger operational requirement.

Por esta razón, antes de pagar, se debe comparar precios, revisar las condiciones de venta y acceder a los comercios desde sus direcciones oficiales.
Cómo saber si un comercio en línea es falsa
Una tienda fraudulenta puede reproducir el diseño, los logotipos y las imágenes de un comercio legítimo. La diferencia suele aparecer en detalles de la dirección web: una letra cambiada, un dominio inusual o una extensión distinta de la oficial.
El Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad de España (INCIBE) sugiere escribir la dirección del comercio en el navegador en lugar de ingresar a través de enlaces recibidos por correo, mensajes de texto o redes sociales.

A developer named Skynizz recently unveiled the Universal Ray Tracing Injector (URTI), an add-on for ReShade designed to further improve graphics realism in PC games. URTI adds another layer of visual fidelity to the popular post-processing injector, bringing real-time ray-traced reflections to DirectX 12 games that were not originally designed to support the effect.
Skynizz explained that URTI can "capture" 3D geometry in DX12 games by replaying every draw call through the stream output. At the end of the rendering pipeline, the game should display its original geometry, including any transformations, with realistic reflections on water, puddles, glass, and other simulated surfaces.
URTI performs its work using Microsoft's official ray tracing API for DirectX 12 games, DXR 1.1. Ray-traced reflections are hardware accelerated, but URTI does not need to modify the game's original assets or shaders. Although it could theoretically support more DXR-based games, URTI is currently focused exclusively on Red Dead Redemption 2.

articles.title: How often should you do maintenance on a Mac?
articles.summary:
Every Mac user knows that the operating system runs very well, and it can give you impressive performance for quite some time. But this is a machine and eventually there can be some problems which arise. Hence the reason why it makes sense to perform some maintenance. Now the question is, how often do you need to perform that maintenance? Here’s what you need to consider.
Does Mac OS maintain itself?
Yes, it does a lot of things in the background, on its own. The idea here is that it automates many tasks like clearing out expired temporary files, rebuilding internal databases or rotating system logs. All of that is made automatically in the background, which makes it incredibly rewarding and exciting as well, something to take into account.
Another thing that Mac OS does is it performs SSD Optimization. It trims the device in order to keep any file fragments close to one another. Doing so improves the overall speed of the device, and it leads to a way better and more consistent experience. Silicon Macs also have better RAM management and a system called unified memory. That’s excellent, and it truly helps enhance the experience in better ways than you might expect.
Things to do on a weekly basis
- A good idea is to wipe down the screen, keyboard and trackpad. It’s very easy for these to get dirty, so cleaning everything up is a very good idea.
- Some people leave their Mac open, and that can lead to all kinds of problems. The best approach is to try and restart your Mac often…

articles.title: Accuracy and Resolution for Magnetic Angle Sensors
articles.summary:
Introduction
Magnetic position sensors, especially magnetic angle sensors, are the fundamental building blocks of countless motion-control applications that necessitate precision positioning. These sensors are pivotal in a wide range of industries, from automotive and robotics to consumer electronics and medical devices, underscoring their universal appeal and importance (see Figure 1).
However, to realize their full potential and utility, one must delve into two crucial parameters that govern their performance: accuracy and resolution. Although these terms are often used interchangeably, they represent distinct — albeit related — concepts in any measuring system. This comprehensive article aims to shed light on these parameters, explain how they impact the performance of magnetic position sensors, and provide guidance on optimizing these factors.
Understanding Accuracy and Resolution
Within the context of measurement and instrumentation, accuracy refers to the closeness of a measured value to the actual or true value of the quantity being measured. For magnetic position sensors, accuracy is the measure of how precisely the sensor’s angle measurement reports the actual angle. Accuracy is a way of understanding how closely the sensor’s read position corresponds to the actual position, with a high accuracy sensor producing readings that are very close to the true position.

articles.title: Etsy clarifies AI terms after seller backlash
articles.summary:
After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.
In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company’s terms of service and admitted that her team “should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content.”
“Our recent terms update was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we’re using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.”
Aaron Meshon, a longtime professional illustrator and Etsy seller, told Ars that even though the company had dialed back its AI language somewhat, the changes were mere “sugar coating.”
He said he still plans on shutting down his 15-year-old Etsy store on December 1.
“I would say I’m losing 20 percent of my yearly income,” he said. “It’s a few mortgage payments.”
He noted that Etsy’s announcement also seems to be rather tone-deaf, given that many retailers make a substantial portion of their annual revenue in the run-up to the end-of-year holiday season.

articles.title: Siempre nos han dicho que parar 15 minutos a hacer ejercicio mejora el estudio. La ciencia dice que no es tan sencillo
articles.summary:
Cuando nos ponemos a estudiar delante de un tocho de apuntes, es fácil que al rato la concentración comience a flaquear. En este caso, levantarse de la silla para hacer 15 minutos de ejercicio moderado es algo que siempre nos han dicho que puede despejarnos y mejorar el rendimiento académico. El problema es que no es tan fácil.
La base. Uno de los pilares habituales para defender los descansos activos viene de un ensayo publicado en 2014. En este un grupo de investigadores evaluó a 123 niños de entre 10 y 11 años de cuatro colegios de primaria tras hacer una hora de deberes. De este modo, cada estudiante pasó por cuatro escenarios distintos: seguir sin pausa, hacer un descanso pasivo, realizar 15 minutos de actividad física moderada o hacer 15 minutos de ejercicio vigoroso.
El resultado determinó que la mejora cognitiva más marcada se daba en el grupo de niños que habían hecho una actividad moderada. Por contra, el ejercicio vigoroso arrojó resultados similares a los que se vieron en hacer un simple descanso pasivo, seguramente por la fatiga que genera.
Tiene sentido. Para explicar cómo el movimiento puede ayudar a fijar todo lo que se ha estudiado, se suele recurrir a un estudio de 2021 donde se analizó todo lo que ocurría en el cerebro cuando se estaba haciendo bicicleta estática. Aquí los investigadores observaron que tanto el ejercicio moderado como el intenso elevaban los niveles de BDNF del cerebro y de anandamida, un endocannabinoide implicado en la plasticidad sinápti…

articles.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia's code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
articles.summary:
When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO.
It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia.
Matt Plass, chief market strategy officer at LRN, an ethics and compliance training outfit, recently surveyed more than 2,000 workers across different industries for a study on workplace codes of conduct. As Plass sees it, the biggest risk is that employees will become ashamed of their workplace.
“People coming into the workforce now, ethics is incredibly important to them,” he told TechCrunch. “They’re really mindful of the ethical standards of their…

articles.summary:
Note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements. Readers interested in this background can find further context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault.
After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it’s an installable package with automatic updating.
Ladybird is most notable for what it isn’t: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google’s Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird’s rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. “The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork,” project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday’s announcement. “The browser around it is modest, but functional.”
A fourth engine
Nearly the entire modern web currently runs on three browser engines. There’s WebKit (Safari), Gecko (Firefox), and the biggest of them all, Blink (Chromium). Those limited options mean that web developers often end up optimizing sites for Chromium specifically, since that’s where the majority of traffic is, and as a result, the whole web platform tends to follow suit toward whatever the dominant engine supports.

In a nutshell: Signal has begun blocking screenshots by default in its messaging app. The change is aimed at AI agents that can read a phone's screen and capture sensitive information in the process. Signal argues that agents built into the operating system can bypass the end-to-end encryption that is the app's main selling point.
The company's concern is where these agents operate. Signal says Google, Apple, and Microsoft are integrating autonomous agents "deep" into their device operating systems. An agent with that level of access does not need to break an app's encryption because it can see messages, pictures, and emails after the app decrypts them for display. Any safeguards built into an individual app can therefore be bypassed.
Udbhav Tiwari, Signal's head of strategy and global affairs, put the stakes in strong terms. "The ability for billions of devices to permanently spy on their users makes the Edward Snowden revelations look like a joke," he told Politico, referring to the 2013 disclosures about mass US government surveillance.
He also raised a potential legal avenue for surveillance. Governments seeking access to private information could ask technology companies for data collected by their agents. That would eliminate the need to break encryption or install malware on a target's phone.
Apple, Google, and Microsoft declined to comment on Signal's claims. Signal wants operating system makers to give apps a way to opt out of AI data access and processing. Blocking …

En clair, ARTEX devait aider les experts en cybersécurité à débusquer les failles avant les pirates. Publié en libre accès sur Github, le logiciel a été promptement détourné par des cybercriminels. Branché sur des modèles d’IA chinois, comme DeepSeek, ARTEX peut orchestrer des attaques en toute autonomie, sans la moindre intervention initiale.
Des pirates s’en sont donc servis pour dérober les données personnelles d’environ 67 000 personnes en s’attaquant à des banques sud-coréennes. Les attaques se sont multipliées jusqu’à ce que le FBI publie une alerte officielle, assurant qu’« ARTEX réduit considérablement le temps nécessaire pour enchaîner les techniques d’attaque, certaines intrusions passant du ciblage initial à un accès privilégié en moins de trois heures ».
Dos au mur, le développeur Autumn-27 n’a pas tardé à retirer ARTEX de GitHub, mais des copies circulent toujours. En dépit de son retrait, ARTEX s’est retrouvé impliqué dans la cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne, qui a obligé l’institution à couper une partie de ses systèmes pendant dix jours. En interne, la Commission soupçonne des pirates soutenus par la Chine.

articles.title: AMD Wants to Ray Trace Large, Dynamic Worlds with Reusable Parts
articles.summary:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
AMD Wants to Ray Trace Large, Dynamic Worlds with Reusable Parts
To scale large, open, dynamic worlds with ray tracing, AMD is developing a new approach to simplify the process. By extending traditional techniques, AMD introduces Ray Tracing Multi-Level Acceleration Structures (RT-MLAS). This technology adds additional levels of reusable acceleration structures within ray-traced objects, reducing both memory consumption and the time required to build and update them. Traditional ray tracing pipelines rely on two levels of acceleration structures: Bottom-Level Acceleration Structures (BLAS), which contain geometry, and a Top-Level Acceleration Structure (TLAS), which organizes instances of that geometry. However, large open worlds can have an enormous number of objects, making the TLAS increasingly expensive to rebuild as objects move or change their level of detail (LOD).
RT-MLAS addresses this challenge by introducing Mid-Level Acceleration Structures (MDLAS), allowing developers to organize objects into additional reusable hierarchies. AMD's implementation supports up to two additional levels, enabling repeated scene components to share acceleration structures rather than being individually duplicated or registered in an increasingly large TLAS. For example, an entire building can be represented by an MDLAS containing reusable walls, windows, doors, and roof components. This approach is particularly useful for open-world environments, where dev…

According to PIBO, Pelee Island “sits on a major bird migration route and within areas where critical habitat is mapped for seven species at risk.”
The group has been asking Canadians to sign a petition calling for the government to block the tower and conduct a full environmental assessment of the project. It also held a media briefing earlier today in which it noted that more than 200,000 birds in Canada are killed by communication towers annually.
DRW, the company behind the tower, told Global News that it’s using “best-in-class” technology to protect wildlife. The tower would be used for a U.S.-based company to trade data between Chicago and New Jersey. PIBO, for its part, says it has received thousands of letters of support for its pleas.
“Pelee Island is one of the stupidist [sic] places on the planet to put such a stock-trading tower,” wrote Atwood on her Substack. “It’s not a wifi tower, it would bring no communications benefits to the Island, and it would seriously tarnish the image of Pelee as a nature and birding oasis. If you wanted to kill a lot of birds with a huge, deadly tower—a LOT of birds — you couldn’t have planned it better.”
Source: PIBO Via: Global News

articles.title: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and 'key man' risks
articles.summary:
S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices.
Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement.
The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale.
Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral.
In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported.
A downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand even larger guarantees.

Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.
Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. AMD's smaller RDNA 4 GPU gets one step closer to 5 GHz.
AMD has set a new GPU overclocking world record by pushing the Radeon RX 9060 XT to 4,837 MHz. Veteran overclocker Bill Alverson and AMD VP Jack Huynh found the limits of this particular chip as part of a celebration of the opening of a new Micro Center location in Austin, Texas. According to the OC World Record Museum database maintained by SkatterBencher, Huynh and Alverson set the new record on November 15.
If you were expecting to see this record from AMD's high-end RX 9070 XT, you're not crazy. The record was indeed achieved using the midrange RDNA 4 part rather than AMD’s flagship GPU. The RX 9060 XT uses a smaller Navi 44 GPU featuring 2,048 shading units (32 compute units), a 160W TDP, 16GB of GDDR6 memory on a 128-bit bus, and a stock boost clock speed of up to 3,130 MHz.
The new frequency record was achieved using liquid nitrogen cooling. At 4,837 MHz, the GPU was running approximately 54.5% faster than its advertised boost frequency. A GPU-Z screenshot confirms the record breaking frequency with the GPU temperature at -49°C, 62W power draw, and voltage at 1.434V.

articles.title: En Jerez, un hombre con tres órdenes judiciales para ir a prisión aparece haciendo ejercicio tranquilamente en el gimnasio de un polígono

Dos años en paradero desconocido. Tres órdenes de ingreso en prisión. Y, aun así, la Policía lo encontró en ese lugar donde cualquiera puede entrar con mochila e ir a su bola: el gimnasio de un polígono. Esconderse de la justicia suena a vida de película pero, en la práctica, suele ser una cuestión de rutinas. En Jerez, tras varias semanas de investigación, ha dado con alguien que llevaba más de dos años siendo buscado por la justicia.
Sobre él pesaban tres órdenes judiciales de búsqueda, detención e ingreso en prisión, emitidas por órganos de Cádiz. Ni su nombre ni su edad constan en la información oficial, y tampoco los procedimientos concretos. Sí consta de qué trata el asunto: de presuntos vuelcos de droga.
¿Un vuelco? Es el robo de un cargamento de droga a otra banda. Los ladrones van armados y a menudo se hacen pasar por policías. Así, los narcos a veces disparan sin saber quién llega. La Guardia Civil los considera sumamente complejos de investigar, porque las víctimas no quieren denunciar que les han robado droga.
Qué dice la ley. Hasta donde se sabe, no existe un delito llamado "vuelco". Los tribunales aplican la maquinaria general: robo con violencia o intimidación (artículo 242 del Código Penal), de dos a cinco años de prisión, en su mitad superior si hay armas. Si actúan varios, suman grupo criminal. Una sentencia de la Audiencia de Zaragoza sobre cinco vuelcos incluía pertenencia a grupo criminal y usurpación de funciones públicas.

articles.title: Google DeepMind AI engineers conjure mathematical proof of Signal's encryption protocol — AlphaProof Code framework powered human-bot cooperation for speedy work
articles.summary:
Google DeepMind AI engineers conjure mathematical proof of Signal's encryption protocol — AlphaProof Code framework powered human-bot cooperation for speedy work
Code tests are one thing, but a mathematical proof is one heck of a security blanket.
A team at Google's DeepMind AI labs has performed a complete formal proof of the code that implements the encryption mechanism for the Signal private chat application. The scientists call their procedure AlphaProof Code and claim it can be applied to other situations requiring complete end-to-end verification of computer code, meaning Signal is safe, and you can find the full paper and the code repository detailing the proof.
More explicitly, the team reviewed an Arm-compiled version of libsignal, the library that the Signal application itself incorporates and uses, with some minimal scaffolding around it. Note that the verification wasn't done against the source code: it was purposely executed against an AArch64 binary, meaning the method can be reused for future verifications of other software.
In a similar vein to the AI labs' work on mathematics, the bulk of the work was done in Lean, a purpose-built language for formal proofs. There's a key difference for this effort, though. Lean is primarily used to prove the underlying math in algorithms, which in this case would be the specifications for Signal's encryption.

Indian SMBs with in-house AI talent grew their teams 5.2 percentage points faster in H1 2026, more than double the global gap. Yet only 6% have everyday AI skills across their workforce, a new Zoho and LinkedIn report finds.

The study covers July 2024 to June 2026. articles.title: Open-weight models are the hottest thing in AI. Are they right for you?
articles.summary:
Open-weight models are the hottest thing in AI. Are they right for you?
For the first three years of the generative artificial intelligence boom, enterprise technology strategy relied on a simple rule: Select the premier frontier foundation model, route every prompt through its commercial application programming interface and pay the subscription premium for access to cutting-edge technology.
That monolithic approach is now collapsing under the weight of operational reality. Open-weight models, AI models whose trained parameters, or “weights,” are publicly available for others to download, run, customize and fine-tune, are the overnight sensation in an industry already moving at light speed.
These models don’t necessarily provide access to their training data, source code or training methods. They also carry a variety of license types that may restrict how they can be used commercially. But they offer choice, flexibility and cost advantages that the leading-edge “frontier” models such as OpenAI Group PBC’s ChatGPT and Anthropic PBC’s Claude don’t. For information technology organizations, they can be a respite from spiraling token costs.
Model overkill
The popularity of these models has soared as AI has matured and organizations have realized that not every use case demands the biggest and best solution. They come in various shapes and sizes, ranging from less than 1 billion to nearly 3 trillion parameters. Many are tuned for specific tasks, such as recognizing images or writ…

Huawei convicted of money laundering, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and fraud by US jury — FBI says Chinese tech giant built its success on deception and theft
The sentencing hearing will not happen until September 2027, though.
A jury has found Huawei guilty of bank fraud, wire fraud, money laundering conspiracy, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and violations of the U.S. sanctions against Iran, among others. According to Bloomberg, the verdict was the result of a nearly three-month trial in which a foreign company has been prosecuted by the U.S. Department of Justice. This is a rare occurrence, resulting in a conviction of 10 out of 12 counts, with the Chinese company getting cleared of conspiracy to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy.
“Today’s verdict makes clear that fraud, sanctions evasion, and the theft of intellectual property are not business strategies, they are serious crimes,” James Barnacle, the Assistant Director in Charge of the FBI New York Field Office, which conducted the investigation on the tech firm, told the publication. “Huawei’s success was built on deception and theft, and the FBI will never hesitate to pursue those who profit by breaking the law.”

Empresa e três subsidiárias também foram consideradas culpadas por fraude bancária, lavagem de dinheiro e violações de sanções contra o Irã.
A Huawei foi considerada culpada pela Justiça dos Estados Unidos por conspiração para roubar segredos comerciais de empresas do país. Além da espionagem, a empresa também foi condenada por fraude bancária, lavagem de dinheiro e violações de sanções contra o Irã.
Segundo o Departamento de Justiça dos EUA (DOJ), outras três subsidiárias da companhia também foram condenadas: Huawei Device, Futurewei Technologies e Huawei Device USA. Apesar disso, o júri absolveu a Huawei das acusações de conspiração para extorsão organizada e de conspiração para obstruir a Justiça.
Em nota, mencionada pela Associated Press, a Huawei comemorou a absolvição nestes pontos e contestou os demais vereditos. “Acreditamos que as acusações restantes do governo também não têm mérito jurídico ou factual”.
As acusações fazem parte de um processo iniciado em 2019, mesmo ano em que os Estados Unidos sancionaram a Huawei por suspeitas de espionagem para a China — o que impede a empresa de negociar com empresas do ocidente há anos. A sentença deve ser determinada em audiência marcada para 14 de setembro de 2027. Em nota, a companhia alega que pretende recorrer.

articles.title: AI Makes Formal Verification Practical
articles.summary:
LONDON, U.K. — Math AI foundation model startup Harmonic is expanding into formal verification for software and hardware, starting with C, Verilog, and Rust.
Formal verification is a well-known technique for proving code is correct, and when extended to hardware description languages such as Verilog, for proving hardware designs are correct and will function exactly as the specification demands. Though it’s well known, formal verification is used in a relatively limited way today, and only by specialists, Harmonic CEO Tudor Achim told EE Times.
There are two main techniques used for formal verification today. Most existing schemes use model checkers, which run the code many times over to explore all the possible states to try to find a state for which the code doesn’t behave as intended. Model checkers are powerful, but as the complexity of hardware increases, they are increasingly compute-intensive.
The other method, theorem proving, creates a logical proof that the implementation of the code is mathematically equivalent to its specification. Until now, this required humans to write proofs, and was very difficult for complex hardware.
“Historically, theorem proving has been horrible compared to model checkers,” Achim said. “Because to write a theorem proving proof, you need to write a lot of language, and to write a model checking proof you just need to solve some very specific algorithmic math problems.”

articles.title: Samsung and SK hynix to License YMTC's Xtacking Technology
articles.summary:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Samsung and SK hynix to License YMTC's Xtacking Technology
According to Nikkei Asia, South Korea's largest chipmakers are currently looking to license technology from China's YMTC. Specifically, SK hynix and Samsung are exploring ways to integrate YMTC's highly successful Xtacking silicon 3D NAND design. In the fourth iteration of Xtacking, YMTC can separate memory cell wafers from peripheral logic circuits and combine them using hybrid bonding wafer-to-wafer stacking. Hybrid bonding creates a permanent bond between two silicon chips using embedded metal bumps that are fused together to form a single chip. Multiple dies or entire silicon wafers can be connected by stacking the back ends of two chips together, and SK hynix and Samsung see this as a potential way to advance their 3D NAND production.
Since 2019, YMTC has been manufacturing using Xtacking technology, now on version 4.0. Samsung told Nikkei Asia that this bonding technology offers numerous advantages over the current approach to building many-layer NAND flash. SK hynix and Samsung are building NAND with hundreds of layers but are hitting single-wafer limitations. YMTC's technology has been refined and production-tested, making it easier for Samsung and SK hynix to switch to it. Additionally, YMTC has filed more than 4,000 patents related to 3D memory production, packaging, and more since 2018. articles.title: VPN familial : attention, tous vos appareils ne sont pas protégés de la même façon

Quel VPN choisir pour un foyer qui utilise Windows, Mac, Android et iPhone ?
Quel VPN pour Windows, Mac, Android et iPhone ? Comparez les fonctions par système, les connexions simultanées et le coût pour équiper votre foyer au mieux.
À la maison, le PC familial tourne sous Windows, un autre ordinateur est un Mac, les enfants utilisent Android et un parent possède un iPhone. Un seul abonnement VPN peut couvrir cet ensemble. Mais retrouver le même logo sur quatre écrans ne garantit pas les mêmes réglages. Les exclusions d’applications, les protections complémentaires et le nombre de connexions autorisées varient. Pour choisir un VPN Windows, Mac, Android et iPhone, il faut donc compter les appareils réellement connectés et identifier les fonctions indispensables sur chacun. Une offre illimitée résout le premier problème ; elle ne suffit pas à régler le second.
Compter les connexions du soir plutôt que les appareils du placard
Prenons un foyer de quatre personnes : deux PC Windows, un Mac, deux smartphones Android, deux iPhone et une tablette. Si les huit appareils utilisent le VPN en même temps, une limite de sept connexions impose de libérer une place. Avec dix, il reste deux connexions disponibles. Ajouter trois appareils actifs porte le besoin à onze et dépasse alors ce plafond. Ce scénario compare des capacités, sans prétendre reproduire les usages de toutes les familles.

Other AI chip stocks have also taken a hit. Broadcom Inc. closed a small fraction of a percent lower than yesterday, while Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Intel Corp. fell 1.6% and 0.6%, respectively.

articles.title: China's memory giants have a record year as Huawei ships HBM without a named source
articles.summary:
The state of China's memory industry in 2026 — CXMT and YMTC are booming, but HBM remains a headache
A record year for Chinese memory, while Huawei ships its own HBM without a named source.
China’s homegrown memory comes largely from two companies, CXMT for DRAM and YMTC for 3D NAND, and both are booming. CXMT’s Oct. 30 quarterly report shows a nine-month net profit of ¥132.0 billion ($19.6 billion), against a ¥5.28 billion ($785 million) loss a year earlier, on revenue more than eight times as high, at ¥269.0 billion ($40.0 billion). YMTC’s numbers, just for Q1, are at ¥47.04 billion ($7.0 billion) in revenue and ¥33.38 billion ($5.0 billion) in profit attributable to shareholders, more than double 2025.
Both are expanding and adding fabs, and each is edging into the other’s products. No Chinese manufacturer can yet produce high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in volume, though. HBM is the stacked DRAM that AI accelerators depend on, and currently the U.S. bars Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron from selling it into China. CXMT’s prospectus lists no HBM project, though its HBM3E is reportedly in risk production, an early run before the process is fully qualified. Huawei designs its own HBM but doesn’t say who makes it.
Memory is a commodity, so the story is in the wafers. We cover the companies running memory fabs in China: CXMT, YMTC, a handful of smaller Chinese fabs, and Samsung and SK hynix, which run some of their biggest plants there. Huawei makes the cut for its HBM program, though…

articles.title: Attacker used 1Password employee's GitHub account to copy customer records
articles.summary:
Attacker used 1Password employee’s GitHub account to copy customer records
Identity security company 1Password today disclosed a security incident in which an attacker, working through an employee’s corporate GitHub account, copied account records belonging to a subset of its customers.
According to the company, the incident came to light on Nov. 19, when 1Password began investigating signs that the GitHub account had been compromised. Using the account, the attacker is said to have pushed malicious code to 1Password’s backend services, which then downloaded what the company describes as “administrative data pertaining to our customers.”
The records taken include names and email addresses, account and user identifiers, account creation and last sign-in times, public keys, Secure Remote Password protocol parameters and other non-secret account metadata. Rounding out the list are tokens found in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery.
Customer vaults, the items stored in them and the keys that protect them were not affected, according to 1Password. “At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker,” the company said in its disclosure. Account passwords and Secret Keys are not stored by the company. Also left untouched, the company says, were account recovery keys and the 1Password apps and browser extensions.
Beyond the customer records, the attacker is said to have copied source code from private repositories.…

articles.title: SpaceX de Elon Musk recibe autorización para lanzar un millón de satélites y crear centros de datos en el espacio
articles.summary:
La Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones de Estados Unidos (FCC) autorizó a SpaceX, la compañía aeroespacial de Elon Musk, a desplegar un millón de satélites para crear una constelación de centros de datos en el espacio.
La autorización permitirá a SpaceX poner en órbita hasta un millón de módulos informáticos de la constelación Starmind, destinados a procesar grandes cantidades de datos que luego se utilizarían en la Tierra.
Según la FCC, se trata de la primera autorización de este tipo en la historia de Estados Unidos.
La agencia estadounidense señaló que el proyecto busca responder a la creciente demanda de capacidad de procesamiento para inteligencia artificial. Los módulos orbitales utilizarían energía solar y operarían de acuerdo con las normas de la FCC sobre desechos espaciales.

As novidades foram anunciadas ontem (24/11) e estão sendo liberadas gradualmente para toda a base acadêmica. A plataforma reúne 10 milhões de currículos cadastrados, dos quais cerca de 2 milhões foram adicionados apenas em 2026, segundo o CNPq.

Le pirate s'est servi de ce compte GitHub pour accéder au code source de 1Password, puis pour installer un code malveillant sur ses serveurs internes. Avec ce code, il a téléchargé des données de comptes clients, avec les noms, les adresses e-mail de connexion, les dates de création et de dernière connexion, ou encore des jetons tirés de certains liens envoyés par e-mail. L'éditeur parle seulement d'un « sous-ensemble » de ses clients. Le nombre de personnes concernées est inconnu, relève The Verge, pour qui cette fuite pourrait exposer les clients à des tentatives de phishing.
1Password allonge les codes envoyés par e-mail
Les jetons volés viennent de liens d'invitation, de création et de récupération de compte. Un jeton sert à finaliser l'invitation ou la récupération, mais seul, il ne donne pas accès au compte, assure 1Password. Il faut aussi une connexion SSO ou un code à six chiffres, envoyé à l'adresse e-mail enregistrée.
